name: Cross-Court Forehand Depth Ladder
summary: Builds a reliable deep cross-court forehand by scoring only rally balls that land behind a throwdown line two metres inside the baseline.
setup: Both players start on the deuce side of their own baseline, between the centre mark and the singles sideline. On each side, lay three throwdowns in a line two metres inside the baseline, spread from the singles sideline to the centre mark, so the strip between the throwdowns and the baseline is the target zone. Ball basket at the near net post for restarts.
instructions: Player A starts the rally with an easy cross-court forehand from a self-drop.
Rally forehand to forehand cross-court, cooperatively, at rally pace.
A ball that lands in the target strip (between the throwdowns and the baseline) scores one for the hitter; a shorter ball scores nothing but the rally continues.
An error ends the rally; restart from the basket, alternating who starts.
First to ten target balls wins the rung; play three rungs, then switch to the ad side and repeat on the backhand.
coaching_points: Aim a racket length above the net tape; depth comes from height, not from hitting harder.
Finish with the racket over the opposite shoulder before you look where the ball went.
Recover to the centre of your half after every ball, not the centre of the court.
Load the outside leg before the bounce so the hip drives the ball up and through.
progressions: Move the throwdown line to one metre inside the baseline.
Score only balls that also land in a two-metre lane along the singles sideline.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Move the throwdown line to the service line so any ball past it scores.
Allow one non-counting recovery ball after each error before the rally must restart.
Use an orange ball.

name: Second Serve Kick Zones
summary: Grooves a second serve that clears the net with margin and lands in the two places a returner least wants it: the wide corner and the T.
setup: Server behind the near baseline, half a metre to the right of the centre mark, serving into the far service box on the left. In that box lay a two-metre square of four cones in the back outside corner, against the service line and the singles sideline, and a single hoop on the T. Basket beside the server. With more than one player, servers take turns from the same spot sharing one basket, and whoever is resting stands behind the far baseline to call where each serve lands.
instructions: Serve ten second serves at the wide-corner cone square, then ten at the T hoop.
Only count a serve that clears the net by at least a racket length; a serve that scrapes the tape is worth nothing here even if it lands in.
Score one for the box, three for a ball that lands inside the cones or the hoop.
After each block of ten, note the score, then serve one block of ten calling the target out loud before the toss.
With two or more players, rotate every ten serves; the resting player calls the landing spot from behind the far baseline.
coaching_points: Toss slightly behind the head and to the left so the racket brushes up the back of the ball.
Lead with the racket edge up to contact; the strings turn the ball over, the arm does not push it.
Snap up at contact, not forward; the ball should climb before it dips.
Land inside the court on the left foot with the right leg kicking back behind you.
progressions: Shrink the cone square from two metres to one.
Alternate targets on every serve without pausing between balls.
Add a returner who must put the ball back cross-court; the serve scores only if the return lands short of the service line.
regressions: Serve from the service line instead of the baseline, same targets.
Use a green ball so the ball slows down and the spin is easier to see.
Remove the T hoop and serve only at the wide-corner square.

name: Wide Forehand Shuttle with Recovery Line
summary: Trains the run to a wide forehand and the recovery back to the middle, with the feeder timing each ball off the hitter's recovery.
setup: Feeder stands two metres inside the near service line on the deuce side with the basket beside them. One cone a metre inside the singles sideline and two metres behind the near service line on the forehand side; a throwdown on the centre mark is the recovery point. Hitter starts on the throwdown. Extra players queue behind the near baseline, outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball to bounce beside the wide cone.
Hitter runs from the throwdown to the cone, hits a cross-court forehand over the net, and recovers to the throwdown with side steps.
Feeder sends the next ball as the hitter touches the throwdown, not before.
Six balls, then the hitter jogs to the back of the queue and the next player steps on.
Three rounds each, then move the cone to the backhand side and repeat.
coaching_points: Split step as the feeder's hand releases the ball.
First step is a big crossover, the last two are small adjustment steps.
Contact out in front of the front hip, then let the racket finish across the body.
Recover with side shuffles facing the net; never turn your back on the feeder.
progressions: Feeder sends the next ball when the hitter is one step from the throwdown, not on it.
Move the cone half a metre closer to the sideline.
Feeder replaces every third wide ball with a short ball inside the service line.
regressions: Move the cone one metre closer to the throwdown.
Feeder waits two full seconds after the hitter stops on the throwdown before the next feed.
Hitter walks the recovery instead of shuffling.

name: Drop-Feed Forehand into the Hoop
summary: Teaches a beginner where the forehand contact point is by hitting self-dropped balls from a marked spot into a hoop across the net.
setup: Player stands on the deuce side just inside the near service line, feet shoulder-width apart, side-on to the net. Place a cone a racket length in front of the front foot and slightly to the right: that is the contact spot. Lay a hoop in the middle of the far service box diagonally across the net. Basket of orange or green balls at the player's feet. A second player, if there is one, stands beside the hoop to collect and roll balls back.
instructions: Hold the ball at arm's length above the cone and drop it, letting it bounce once.
Swing low to high and hit the ball at the top of its bounce, above the cone.
Aim to land the ball in the hoop; count hoops out of ten.
After ten balls, collect (or swap with the collector) and go again.
Three sets of ten, then move the cone one step further forward and hit one more set.
coaching_points: Drop the ball, do not throw it down; it should bounce to hip height.
Turn the shoulders before the ball bounces so the racket is already back.
Hit the ball above the cone, level with the front hip.
Finish with the racket pointing at the hoop, then up over the shoulder.
progressions: Move the hoop to the back corner of the far service box.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
Drop the ball from waist height instead of shoulder height so there is less time to swing.
regressions: Replace the hoop with a two-metre cone square.
Stand one metre inside the service line so the hoop is closer.
Use a red ball for a slower, higher bounce.

name: Hand-Feed Backhand, Return to the Catcher
summary: Pairs a gentle underarm feed with a controlled backhand that must be hit softly enough for the feeder to catch after one bounce.
setup: Feeder stands on the far side just inside the service line, on the centre line, with a basket of orange or green balls beside them. Hitter stands on the near side in the middle of the ad service box, side-on, holding the racket with both hands in a backhand grip. Nothing else on court: the feeder's hands are the target.
instructions: Feeder tosses underarm over the net so the ball bounces once about a metre in front of the hitter's backhand side.
Hitter steps in and hits a backhand back over the net, aiming at the feeder's chest.
Feeder tries to catch the ball after one bounce without moving more than one step; a clean catch scores a point for the pair.
Ten feeds, then swap roles.
Play to twenty points as a pair, then repeat with the hitter starting one step further back.
coaching_points: Step across with the right foot so the shoulder faces the net before the bounce.
Both hands stay on the racket until the ball has left the strings.
Hit at the top of the bounce, in front of the front knee.
Keep the follow-through low and towards the feeder; a big finish sends it long.
progressions: Feeder catches without letting the ball bounce.
Feeder tosses to the backhand or the forehand without warning.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Feeder tosses from the same side of the net, three metres in front of the hitter.
Count any ball that lands in the far service box, not only catches.
Use a red ball for a slower, higher bounce.

name: Service-Box Rally to Ten
summary: Builds rally consistency with a cooperative mini-tennis rally inside the service boxes, counting consecutive balls before the court is opened up.
setup: One player in each service box straight across the net from each other, both starting on their service line at the centre. Play only inside the two boxes: a ball landing past the service line or outside the singles sideline is out. Basket at the net post for quick restarts. Orange or green balls.
instructions: Player A starts with a gentle self-drop hit; the pair rallies cooperatively, forehands or backhands as the ball comes.
Count each ball out loud; the rally ends on an error or a ball outside the boxes.
A rally that reaches ten banks one 'ten'; the pair aims for three tens in the time.
Once three tens are banked, play the next round forehands only, then backhands only, moving round the ball when needed.
Finish with one round where every ball must cross the net at least a racket length above the tape.
coaching_points: Racket back as soon as you see which side the ball is coming to.
Swing low to high and stop the racket at shoulder height; a short swing keeps the ball in the box.
Move your feet to the ball, then hit; no reaching.
Aim for your partner's forehand hip so they can keep it going.
progressions: Extend the playing area two metres behind each service line.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
Each player must alternate forehand and backhand strictly.
regressions: Allow the ball to bounce twice.
Use a red ball.
Feed every third ball by hand instead of hitting it.

name: Call the Gate: Forehand Cross or Line
summary: Teaches beginners to direct the forehand on purpose by hitting through one of two cone gates called by the feeder just before the feed.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line, basket beside them, facing the hitter. Hitter on the near baseline on the deuce side, a metre inside the singles sideline. On the far side lay two cone gates, each two cones three metres apart, both a metre inside the far baseline: one gate cross-court in the far left half and one down the line in the far right half. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder calls 'cross' or 'line', then tosses underarm to bounce a metre in front of the hitter's forehand.
Hitter hits the forehand through the called gate.
One point for the right gate, minus one for the wrong gate, nothing for a miss.
Eight balls each, then rotate: hitter to the back of the queue, next player in.
Second round: the feeder calls the gate only as the ball leaves the hand.
coaching_points: Aim with the feet: the front foot points at the gate you were given.
For cross-court hit the ball a little earlier and further in front; for the line let it come a little later.
Same swing for both directions; change the contact point, not the swing.
Look at the gate before the feed, then eyes on the ball until it hits the strings.
progressions: Narrow each gate from three metres to two.
Feeder calls the gate only after the bounce.
Feeder alternates forehand and backhand feeds, gates unchanged.
regressions: Widen each gate to four metres.
Feeder calls the same gate for four balls in a row before switching.
Feed from three metres in front of the hitter on the same side of the net instead of from the net.

name: Bounce-Hit Rhythm Toss
summary: Fixes timing for the youngest beginners by having them call 'bounce' and 'hit' out loud on every tossed ball before they swing.
setup: Hitter stands on a cone placed on the near service line in the middle of the deuce side, side-on to the net. Feeder crouches three metres in front of the hitter on the same side of the net, a little towards the forehand side, with a basket of red balls. A second cone marks the bounce spot: one metre in front of the hitter and a racket length to the forehand side. A third player, if there is one, waits behind the baseline and collects.
instructions: Feeder tosses underarm so the ball bounces on the bounce cone.
Hitter shouts 'bounce' as the ball bounces and 'hit' as they hit it over the net.
Any ball over the net and inside the far service boxes scores one.
Ten forehands, then ten backhands with the bounce cone moved to the other side, then swap roles or bring in the waiting player.
Last round: the hitter says nothing out loud and the feeder listens for the same rhythm in the swing.
coaching_points: Say 'bounce' the moment the ball touches the ground, not after.
Racket back on 'bounce', swing on 'hit'.
Hit the ball when it is at its highest, level with your hip.
Stay on your cone; the toss comes to you.
progressions: Move the feeder back to five metres so the ball arrives faster.
Switch from a red ball to an orange ball.
Feeder alternates forehand and backhand tosses without moving the bounce cone.
regressions: Feeder tosses from one metre away and lets the ball bounce twice.
Hitter catches the ball in the free hand on 'hit' before progressing to swinging.
Feeder says 'bounce, hit' out loud together with the hitter.

name: Over the Service Line Depth Rally
summary: Turns a beginner baseline rally into a depth game by scoring only balls that land between the service line and the baseline.
setup: One player on each baseline, starting on the centre mark. Lay four throwdowns along each service line, spread evenly between the singles sidelines, so the line is easy to see from the other end. Basket of green balls at the net post.
instructions: Start each rally with an underarm hand-feed from the baseline.
Rally cooperatively down the middle; a ball landing past the throwdowns scores one for the hitter.
A ball landing short of the throwdowns stays in play but scores nothing.
Rally to an error, then restart; first to fifteen deep balls wins.
Second game: score only deep balls hit on the backhand.
coaching_points: Aim two racket lengths above the net; at this level deep balls are high balls.
Take the racket back as the ball leaves your partner's strings.
Hit through the ball towards the far fence, then finish high.
Back to the centre mark after every ball.
progressions: Add a second throwdown line two metres inside the baseline and score only balls that land behind it.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
Play the point out instead of cooperating once the rally passes four balls.
regressions: Move both players in to two metres inside the baseline.
Use an orange ball.
Allow the ball to bounce twice.

name: Forehand-Only Box Points
summary: Competitive points inside the service boxes where only forehands count, forcing beginners to move around the ball early.
setup: One player on each side, starting on the service line at the centre. The playing area is the two service boxes only; place a cone on each singles sideline where it meets the service line, on both sides of the net, so the corners are obvious. Basket at the net post. Green or yellow balls.
instructions: Server starts each point with an underarm hand-feed from the service line; the serve changes hands every two points.
Play the point inside the boxes; a ball hit with the backhand loses the point immediately.
Players may run around the backhand side to hit a forehand; the ball can still land anywhere in the boxes.
First to seven points, change ends, play again.
Third game: the winner of the previous point must hit their next ball cross-court.
coaching_points: Decide 'forehand' before the ball crosses the net and start moving then.
Shuffle sideways around the ball; do not cross your feet on the last step.
Keep the swing short and finish over the shoulder; power loses points in a small box.
Recover to the centre of the box before admiring the shot.
progressions: Extend the area two metres behind each service line.
Backhands are allowed but score half a point.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Rally cooperatively to five before the point becomes live.
Use an orange ball.
Allow one backhand per point without penalty.

name: Basket Rhythm: Forehand, Backhand, Repeat
summary: Grooves the basic forehand and backhand swings with a steady basket feed that alternates sides on every ball, with a queue rotating in.
setup: Feeder on the near side, two metres inside the service line on the centre line, with the basket beside them. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. Lay one large target in the middle of each far half, two metres inside the far baseline. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline; the first in the queue collects stray balls.
instructions: Feeder tosses underarm at a steady rhythm of one ball every three seconds, alternating forehand side and backhand side, each ball bouncing a metre in front of the hitter.
Hitter hits every forehand cross-court at the far left target and every backhand cross-court at the far right target.
Feeder counts target hits out loud; the hitter tries to beat their own score from the previous round.
Ten balls, then the hitter jogs to the back of the queue and the next player steps to the centre mark.
Three rounds each; in the final round the feeder speeds up to one ball every two seconds.
coaching_points: Turn the shoulders before the bounce; taking the racket back is a shoulder turn, not an arm lift.
Step into the ball with the front foot pointing at the target.
Contact level with the front hip, out in front.
One step back to the centre mark between balls; the next feed is already coming.
progressions: Speed the feed up to one ball every two seconds.
Shrink the targets from two metres to one.
Feeder mixes forehands and backhands in an unpredictable order instead of alternating.
regressions: Slow the feed to one ball every five seconds.
Feed the same side ten times before changing.
Use an orange ball.

name: Backhand Cross-Court: Deep, Short, Deep
summary: Builds length control on the backhand by alternating a deep and a short cross-court ball on every shot of a cooperative rally.
setup: Both players on the ad side of their own baseline, between the centre mark and the singles sideline, so the rally is backhand cross-court for right-handers. Lay two throwdowns on each service line at the edges of the ad half so the line is obvious from the far end. The channel is the two ad halves; a ball landing in a deuce half is out. Basket at the net post.
instructions: Player A starts with a self-drop backhand cross-court that must land past the service line.
Player B answers with a backhand that lands inside the service line, then A hits deep again, so every ball alternates deep, short, deep.
Rally cooperatively; a ball to the wrong depth ends the rally.
Count the rally length, then restart from the basket with the other player starting.
Swap who hits deep and who hits short every five rallies.
coaching_points: For the deep ball, finish high with the hands above the shoulder.
For the short ball, shorten the swing and hold the finish at waist height.
Same preparation for both: shoulders turned before the bounce.
Move the feet to set up behind the ball; length comes from the legs, not the arm.
progressions: Short balls must land inside a two-metre strip just over the net, marked with a second throwdown line.
Alternate deep, deep, short instead of every other ball.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Play only deep balls until ten in a row are managed, then add the short ball.
Move both players two metres inside the baseline.
Use an orange ball.

name: Inside-Out Forehand from the Backhand Corner
summary: Teaches the run-around forehand by feeding to the backhand side and asking for an inside-out forehand into the far corner box.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket. Hitter starts a metre behind the near baseline on the centre mark. A cone two metres to the backhand side of the centre mark, a metre inside the baseline, marks where feeds bounce. On the far side, a two-metre cone box in the back corner diagonally opposite the hitter's backhand corner, against the far baseline and the far singles sideline. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses to bounce on the backhand-side cone.
Hitter runs around the ball, sets up outside it and hits an inside-out forehand into the far cone box.
Recover to the centre mark with side steps before the next feed.
Ten balls, then rotate; score one per box hit.
Third round: every fourth feed goes to the forehand side instead, and the hitter must hit that one cross-court to the other corner.
coaching_points: Get around the ball early: three quick steps to the left before the bounce.
Contact out in front and to the side, hips open to the target corner.
Aim over the centre strap, the lowest part of the net, to the deep corner.
Recover along the baseline, not towards the net.
progressions: Shrink the cone box from two metres to one.
Feeder sends the next ball as the hitter passes the centre mark on recovery.
Feed with a racket from the far baseline instead of a hand toss from the net.
regressions: Move the feed cone one metre closer to the centre mark.
Widen the target to the whole far half.
Feeder waits until the hitter is still before tossing.

name: Cross-Court Channel Points to Eleven
summary: Competitive points confined to the cross-court channel, so every ball is a cross-court decision under pressure.
setup: Both players on the deuce side of their own baseline. Place a cone on each baseline at the centre mark and on each service line at the centre line, so the deuce half on each side is clearly marked. The playing area is the two deuce halves only; the doubles alley counts as in. Basket at the net post. After each game the players switch to the ad halves.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed from the baseline, alternating who feeds every two points.
Play the point cross-court only: any ball landing outside the deuce halves loses the point.
First to eleven, win by two.
Second game on the ad halves, backhand cross-court for right-handers.
Third game: the point can be won only with a ball that lands past the service line.
coaching_points: Aim through the middle of your half, a metre inside the sideline; the sideline is not the target.
Recover to the middle of your half, not the middle of the court.
Take the ball on the way up when it lands short and step into it.
Hit high and heavy when you are pulled wide; hit flatter when you are set.
progressions: Shrink the channel to the singles half only, alley out.
Points can be won only after the fourth ball.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Play cooperatively for four balls before the point goes live.
Count the alley and one metre beyond the baseline as in.
Use an orange ball.

name: Depth on Call: Short or Deep Cross-Court
summary: Trains length control on demand by having the feeder call a short or deep zone as each ball is fed.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline on the deuce side. Two zones marked on the far deuce half (the far half on the viewer's left) with throwdowns: a short zone between the net and a throwdown line two metres inside the far service line, and a deep zone between a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline and the baseline. A cone on the far singles sideline at the service line marks the split. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder calls 'short' or 'deep' as the ball leaves the racket, feeding a medium-pace ball to the hitter's forehand.
Hitter hits cross-court into the called zone.
Two points for the zone, one for anywhere else in the far deuce half, zero for a miss.
Ten balls, then rotate the hitter.
Second round: the feeder calls the zone only after the bounce.
coaching_points: Short ball: lift it higher over the net and finish the swing early at waist height.
Deep ball: hit through the ball with the finish above the shoulder.
Hear the call, then set the racket height before the ball arrives.
Recover to the centre mark after every ball.
progressions: Narrow each zone to one metre by moving the throwdown lines.
Feeder alternates forehand and backhand feeds, zones unchanged.
Feeder calls the zone only as the ball bounces.
regressions: Widen the deep zone to everything past the service line.
Feeder calls the same zone for five balls in a row.
Feeder tosses underarm from the far service line instead of hitting with the racket.

name: Figure-of-Eight Rally: Cross-Court vs Down the Line
summary: One player hits everything cross-court and the other everything down the line, so both learn to change direction and recover on the move.
setup: One player on each baseline, starting on the centre mark. Player A hits every ball cross-court; player B hits every ball down the line, so the ball travels in a figure of eight around the court. Basket at the net post. No other equipment: the singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Player A starts with an easy self-drop cross-court.
B returns it down the line; A hits the next one cross-court again, and so on.
Rally cooperatively at a pace both can sustain, aiming past the service line.
Count balls; a rally of twelve banks a point, first to three points.
Switch roles every three minutes: the cross-court player becomes the line player.
coaching_points: Down the line: contact a fraction later and keep the racket face pointing at the target longer.
Cross-court: contact further in front and let the hips open.
You know where the next ball is going, so recover past the centre mark towards it.
Take a small adjustment step just before the swing to set the hitting distance.
progressions: Both players must land the ball past the service line for it to count.
Switch roles every eight balls without stopping the rally.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Move both players two metres inside the baseline.
Restart from a hand-feed after any error and keep the count going.
Use an orange ball.

name: Ball Machine: Six Deep Balls, Hold the Baseline
summary: Uses a ball machine to groove a neutral baseline rhythm, scoring only balls that land in the deep zone.
setup: Ball machine on the far baseline at the centre, set to a medium pace with no spin, alternating forehand and backhand sides at a five-second interval. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline marks the deep zone: balls landing between it and the baseline count. A second player, if present, stands behind the far baseline calling deep or short and collects while the machine reloads.
instructions: Hitter plays six balls, alternating forehand and backhand, aiming every ball into the deep zone.
Count deep balls out of six, then step off while the partner resets or the machine reloads.
Five sets of six; try to beat the previous set's count.
Between sets, walk back to the centre mark and set the ready position before the first ball.
Last set: hit every ball cross-court instead of down the middle.
coaching_points: Split step as the ball leaves the machine.
Hit through the ball with the racket finishing above the shoulder; height gives depth.
Make the last step to the ball a small one so you are not jammed.
Recover to the centre mark between balls with side steps.
progressions: Shorten the machine interval to three seconds.
Add topspin on the machine so the ball kicks up above shoulder height.
Move the deep line to one metre inside the baseline.
regressions: Slow the machine to a seven-second interval.
Move the hitter one metre inside the baseline.
Widen the deep zone to everything past the service line.

name: Short Ball Attack: Step In and Drive Deep
summary: Teaches players to move forward on a short ball and drive it deep down the line instead of pushing it back.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket, facing the hitter. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. A cone one metre inside the near service line on each side of the centre line marks where the short feeds bounce. On the far side, a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline across the whole court marks the deep zone. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses a short ball to bounce on one of the two cones.
Hitter moves forward, drives the ball down the line into the deep zone, and recovers backwards to the baseline with small steps.
Score one for a deep-zone ball, zero for anything short or out.
Eight balls, alternating cones, then rotate the hitter.
Second round: the hitter follows the ball in and the feeder tosses a volley to finish.
coaching_points: Move in early and take the ball at waist height, not after it has dropped.
Contact in front of the front foot with the weight moving forward through the shot.
Aim high over the net; the deep zone needs height, not speed.
After the shot, hold the balance for a beat before recovering.
progressions: Move the deep line to one metre inside the baseline.
Feeder tosses the short ball lower so it must be taken below net height.
Add a one-metre lane along the sideline as the only target.
regressions: Widen the deep zone to everything past the far service line.
Feeder tosses higher and slower.
Hitter starts from the service line instead of the baseline.

name: Three-Height Rally: Low, Medium, High
summary: Develops control of trajectory by rallying at a called net clearance and changing it on command.
setup: Two players rallying straight down one half of the court, both starting a metre inside their own baseline on the same side of the centre line. Basket at the net post. No other equipment: the heights are judged against the net tape (low: within a racket length above the tape; medium: one to two racket lengths; high: more than two).
instructions: Player A calls a height before hitting each ball: low, medium or high.
Player B returns at the same height; the pair rallies cooperatively at that height for five balls.
After five balls A calls a new height and the rally continues without stopping.
A ball at the wrong height ends the rally; restart from the basket with B calling.
Ten minutes, keeping a tally of the longest rally at each height.
coaching_points: Low ball: close the racket face slightly and finish across the body.
High ball: open the face a touch and finish above the head.
Same swing speed for every height; change the face and the finish, not the effort.
Stay a metre inside the baseline so the high ball is taken before it climbs.
progressions: Call the height for the partner's next ball instead of your own.
Change the height every two balls instead of five.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Use only two heights: medium and high.
Rally from the service lines instead of the baselines.
Feed each ball by hand at the called height before hitting live.

name: Cross-Court Corner Box: Ten in a Row
summary: Builds cross-court forehand accuracy under a consecutive-hit count into a three-metre corner box.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline on the deuce side. In the far back corner of the cross-court channel (the far corner on the viewer's left), a three-metre cone box against the baseline and the singles sideline. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder hits medium-pace balls to the hitter's forehand at a rally rhythm.
Hitter hits every ball cross-court into the cone box.
Count consecutive box hits; a miss resets the count to zero.
The set ends when the hitter reaches ten in a row or after thirty balls, then rotate.
Second time through, the feeder varies the depth of the feed between the service line and the baseline.
coaching_points: Aim for the middle of the box, not the corner; the lines are for the opponent.
Brush up the back of the ball so it can go high over the net and still come down in the box.
Set the feet early: the last step is a small one, out to the side of the ball.
Recover to the centre mark after every ball even though the next one is going to the same place.
progressions: Shrink the box to two metres.
Feeder adds a short ball every fourth feed; it must still go into the box.
Feeder feeds at match pace.
regressions: Widen the box to four metres.
Feeder tosses underarm from the far service line.
Count box hits out of ten instead of consecutive hits.

name: Cross-Court Backhand: Slice, Topspin, Slice
summary: Pairs a slicing player with a driving player on the backhand cross-court so both learn to handle and produce the other spin.
setup: Both players on the ad side of their own baseline, starting a metre behind the baseline, so the rally is backhand cross-court for right-handers. The channel is the two ad halves; the singles sideline and the centre line are the boundaries. Basket at the net post. No cones: the ball's flight is the feedback.
instructions: Player A starts with a self-drop backhand slice cross-court.
Player B replies with a topspin backhand; A slices again, B drives again, so one player slices all rally and the other drives.
Rally cooperatively for twelve balls, then swap roles without stopping if possible.
A slice that floats above shoulder height, or a topspin that lands short of the service line, ends the rally.
Keep a tally of the longest rally in each role.
coaching_points: Slice: high to low with the racket face open, finishing with the racket pointing at the target.
Topspin: drop the racket head below the ball and brush up, finishing over the shoulder.
Same shoulder turn for both; the difference is the racket path, not the preparation.
Against the slice, bend the knees and get under the low ball before swinging up.
progressions: The slice must land past the service line to count.
Swap roles every four balls, called by the slicer.
The topspin player takes every ball on the rise from inside the baseline.
regressions: Rally topspin to topspin for ten balls first, then introduce the slice.
Move both players two metres inside the baseline.
Feed the first three balls by hand before the rally goes live.

name: Cross-Court Push-Back: Score by Where They Hit It
summary: Rewards heavy, deep cross-court hitting by scoring every ball that forces the partner to make contact from behind a cone line.
setup: Both players on the deuce side of their own baseline. Behind each baseline, lay a line of three cones two metres back across the deuce half, so there is a visible 'pushed back' line behind the court on both ends. Basket at the net post. Singles lines are the boundaries; the channel is the two deuce halves.
instructions: Rally cross-court forehands at match pace but cooperatively: no winners.
You score a point every time your partner makes contact from behind their cone line.
A ball that lands short, inside the service line, costs you a point.
Play to fifteen, then switch to the ad side for backhands.
Restart every error from the basket, alternating the starter.
coaching_points: Heavy topspin high over the net pushes them back more than a flat hard ball.
Load the legs and lift; the ball should peak on their side of the net.
Take the ball early when you can, so they have less time to get in.
Recover to the middle of your half quickly; a deep ball back at you is coming.
progressions: Score only when your partner is pushed back on the backhand side.
Move the cone lines to three metres behind the baseline.
Allow a short ball to be attacked down the line to end the rally.
regressions: Move the cone lines to one metre behind the baseline.
Score every ball that lands past the service line instead of only pushed-back contacts.
Allow one recovery ball after each error before the rally restarts.

name: Change of Direction on the Short Ball
summary: Turns a cooperative cross-court rally live the moment a ball lands short, training the down-the-line change of direction as a decision.
setup: One player on each baseline, both on the deuce side. Throwdowns along each service line make the short zone, inside the service line, obvious from the far end. Basket at the net post. The rally is cross-court until a ball lands short; the singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Rally cross-court forehands cooperatively.
The moment a ball lands inside the service line, the receiver may change direction down the line and the point is live.
Play the point out; the down-the-line ball must land past the far service line or it loses the point.
First to ten points, then switch to the ad side for backhands.
Restart every point cooperatively from the basket.
coaching_points: Read the short ball early: as soon as it peaks on your side, move in.
Down the line: hold the racket face towards the target longer and hit slightly later.
Keep the change-of-direction ball deep and only as hard as you can control; the point is not over yet.
After changing direction, recover towards the middle, not back to the deuce corner.
progressions: The down-the-line ball must also land inside a two-metre lane along the sideline.
Allow the change of direction on any ball landing within two metres behind the service line as well.
Start points from a serve instead of a hand-feed.
regressions: The short ball may be attacked cross-court or down the line.
Cooperate for three balls after the change before the point becomes live.
Use throwdowns two metres behind the service line as the short zone, so more balls qualify.

name: Ball Machine: Take It on the Rise
summary: Trains early contact by playing every machine ball from inside the baseline before it reaches waist height.
setup: Ball machine on the far baseline at the centre, medium pace with light topspin, alternating sides every four seconds. Hitter starts a metre inside the near baseline on the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline marks the deep target. A second player, if present, calls 'rise' or 'late' from behind the far baseline on each contact.
instructions: Hitter plays every ball from inside the baseline, contacting the ball as it rises, before it reaches waist height.
Aim deep past the far throwdown line; count deep balls out of eight.
Four sets of eight, walking back to the start spot before each set.
Third set every ball cross-court; fourth set every ball down the line.
Between sets, the partner reports how many contacts were late.
coaching_points: Shorten the backswing: racket back to hip level, not behind the body.
Contact out in front with a firm wrist; let the ball's pace do the work.
Stay low through contact so the rising ball does not climb over the strings.
Split step as the machine releases, then a small step forward into the ball.
progressions: Start two metres inside the baseline.
Shorten the machine interval to three seconds.
Increase the machine's topspin so the ball rises faster.
regressions: Start on the baseline instead of inside it.
Slow the machine to a six-second interval with no spin.
Count any ball past the service line as deep.

name: Backhand Down the Line: The Passing Lane
summary: Trains the down-the-line backhand pass into a marked lane while a feeder at the net plays the part of the volleyer.
setup: Feeder at the near net just on the backhand side of the centre line, with the basket, playing the part of a net player. Hitter on the near baseline on the ad side, a metre inside the singles sideline. On the far side, a two-metre lane along the far singles sideline on the hitter's down-the-line side, marked with cones at the service line and the baseline. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses a medium-depth ball to the hitter's backhand, then holds a ready position at the net like a volleyer.
Hitter drives the backhand down the line into the lane, past the feeder's reach.
Score two for the lane, one for anywhere past the far service line on that side, zero if the feeder could have touched it.
Eight balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder takes one step towards the line after each toss to close the lane.
coaching_points: Contact slightly later than cross-court, level with the front hip, face towards the lane.
Hit through the ball with a long finish towards the target; do not roll the wrist early.
A racket length over the net is enough; the lane is long, not high.
Step forward into the shot so the ball is struck moving through, not from a static base.
progressions: Narrow the lane to one metre.
Feeder volleys any ball inside reach back at the hitter and the point continues.
Feeder tosses shorter so the hitter must move in before the pass.
regressions: Widen the lane to three metres.
Feeder stays fixed at the centre line without covering.
Feeder tosses higher and slower to the backhand.

name: High Ball Forehand: Take It Early or Step Back
summary: Gives players two answers to the high looping ball, an early contact above the shoulder or a step back to let it drop, and trains the decision.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, feeding high, loopy balls with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline on the deuce side. A throwdown a metre inside the near baseline marks the 'early' contact line; a second throwdown two metres behind the baseline marks the 'step back' line. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder loops a high ball to bounce near the hitter's baseline on the forehand side.
Hitter either steps in and takes it early from the front throwdown, or steps back behind the rear throwdown and lets it drop; the feeder calls which before the feed.
Hit cross-court past the far service line.
Eight balls, four early and four back, then rotate.
Second round: the hitter chooses and calls it themselves.
coaching_points: Early: contact above the shoulder with the racket face closed, hit down and through.
Back: get behind the bounce, let it drop to shoulder height, and lift with topspin.
Decide before the ball crosses the net; a late decision leaves you jammed.
Keep the elbow high on the high contact so the ball does not sail.
progressions: Feeder varies the feed height so the hitter must decide by the flight.
Early balls must land in the far corner box.
Feeder follows a high ball with a fast flat one.
regressions: Feeder feeds from the far baseline with an underarm loop so the ball is slower.
Only step back for the first round; add the early option once the ball is going in.
Widen the target to anywhere past the net.

name: Backhand Slice: Low Through the Lane
summary: Builds a penetrating backhand slice that stays low over the net and carries deep, using a cone gate and a depth line as feedback.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline on the ad side. Two cones on the near side a metre in front of the net, a metre apart, on the backhand cross-court line: the slice must pass between them and below head height. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline across the far ad half marks the depth target. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder hits a medium-pace ball to the hitter's backhand.
Hitter slices cross-court, low through the cone gate, to land past the far throwdown line.
Score one for the gate, one for the depth, two if both.
Ten balls, then rotate.
Second round: alternate one slice and one topspin drive, both through the gate.
coaching_points: Racket above the ball at the start, then drive forward and slightly down through contact.
Keep the face open but the path flat; a chopping swing floats.
Finish with the racket and the free arm pulling apart for balance.
Stay low through the shot; standing up early lifts the ball over the gate.
progressions: Narrow the gate to half a metre.
Feeder feeds low skidding slices instead of topspin.
Move the depth line to one metre inside the baseline.
regressions: Remove the gate and score depth only.
Feeder tosses underarm from the far service line.
Hitter starts at the service line.

name: Half-Court Points: The Forehand Must Win
summary: Live points down one half of the court where only a forehand can end the point, forcing early run-around decisions.
setup: Both players on the same half of the court lengthways, one each side of the net: the playing area runs from singles sideline to centre line and baseline to baseline. Cones on each baseline and each service line at the centre line mark the inside boundary. Basket at the net post.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed from the baseline, alternating who feeds every two points.
Play the point out inside the half; a point can only be won with a forehand winner or an error forced by a forehand.
A point ended by a backhand winner or a backhand-forced error is replayed.
First to eleven, then play the other half so the run-around forehand becomes the weapon.
Third game: the winning forehand must also be hit from inside the baseline to count.
coaching_points: Move around the backhand early: decide as the ball leaves their racket.
Use the inside-out forehand to open the court, then finish inside-in.
Recover a step towards the backhand side of your half so more balls become forehands.
Change the height, not just the direction; a heavy high ball earns the short reply you want.
progressions: The winning forehand must land past the service line.
Each player may hit only two backhands per point.
Start each point with a serve instead of a hand-feed.
regressions: Any point ended by a forehand counts, forced or not.
Cooperate for four balls before the point goes live.
Play on the whole court, but only forehand winners count.

name: Two-on-One: Backhand Corner Defence
summary: Two attackers pin one defender in the backhand corner so the defender learns to hold the rally from behind the baseline.
setup: Defender on the near baseline in the backhand corner, on the ad side. Two attackers on the far baseline, one on each half, with the basket between them at the centre. A cone on the near singles sideline two metres inside the baseline marks the defender's outside limit. The defender plays only the near ad half; the attackers use the whole far court.
instructions: Attacker one starts with a heavy ball into the backhand corner.
Defender hits every ball back with a backhand, alternating cross-court and down the line, and recovers to the corner cone after each shot.
Attackers hit straight back into the corner at match pace, each trying to hit the next ball harder than the last.
Twelve balls or until an error, then rotate: defender to attacker one, attacker one to attacker two, attacker two to defender.
Score the defender's rally length; best of three rounds each.
coaching_points: Contact out in front even when stretched; a late backhand from the corner floats.
Slice when pushed behind the baseline, drive when the ball sits up.
Recover with crossover steps, then split as the attacker makes contact.
Aim the cross-court deep to the attacker's backhand so their next ball is not an attack.
progressions: Attackers may hit one drop shot per rally.
Defender must land every ball past the far service line to keep the rally alive.
Attackers alternate corners so the defender covers the whole baseline.
regressions: Attackers hit at three-quarter pace.
Defender may hit any shot, not only the backhand.
Defender starts a metre inside the corner cone so the balls are shorter.

name: Backhand Disguise: Slice or Drive from the Same Shape
summary: Trains a backhand preparation that hides whether a slice or a drive is coming, with a caller scoring how late the shot is read.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket into the near ad half. Hitter on the near baseline on the ad side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline across the far cross-court half marks the depth target for both shots. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline; the first in the queue stands behind the feeder as the caller.
instructions: Feeder hits medium-pace balls to the backhand at a rally rhythm.
Hitter alternates slice and topspin drive in any order they choose, cross-court, past the depth line.
The caller behind the feeder shouts which shot is coming as soon as they can tell; the hitter scores a point every time the call comes after contact.
Ten balls, then rotate all three roles.
Second round: the hitter must hit two of one shot before switching.
coaching_points: Same unit turn and same racket height on the take-back for both shots; the split happens in the last half metre.
Drive: drop the racket head late and brush up; slice: keep it above the ball and drive forward.
Keep the eyes and the front shoulder still through contact so nothing gives the shot away.
Both shots deep: a disguised short ball is still a short ball.
progressions: The caller must call before the ball bounces on the hitter's side.
Feeder mixes in a short ball; the hitter must still disguise the reply.
Add the drop shot as a third option from the same shape.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm so the hitter has more time to shape the swing.
Hitter announces the sequence before the ten balls and works on the shape only.
Remove the depth line and score disguise only.

name: Deep Ball Pick-Up: Half-Volley from the Baseline
summary: Teaches players to hold the baseline against deep balls by taking them on the half-volley instead of retreating.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, driving deep balls with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown a metre behind the baseline marks the line the hitter may not retreat behind. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline and collect.
instructions: Feeder drives balls to land within a metre of the near baseline, alternating sides.
Hitter takes every ball on the half-volley or just after the bounce, without retreating behind the throwdown.
Aim deep down the middle past the far service line; count balls in out of ten.
Ten balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder adds pace and the hitter blocks instead of swings.
coaching_points: Racket below the ball early, knees bent, so the short hop is met with a firm face.
Shorten the swing to a block; the ball's pace is enough.
Contact in front of the front foot; a half-volley taken beside the body pops up.
Keep the head still and low through contact; standing up lifts the ball long.
progressions: Hitter must stand a metre inside the baseline.
Feeder mixes topspin and slice so the bounce height changes.
Target the far corners instead of the middle.
regressions: Feeder feeds at three-quarter pace.
Move the throwdown two metres behind the baseline so the hitter may step back.
Feeder tells the hitter which side before each feed.

name: Heavy Cross-Court, Flat Down the Line
summary: Pairs a heavy topspin cross-court rally with a flat down-the-line change into a narrow lane, live from the moment someone changes.
setup: One player on each baseline, both on the deuce side. Throwdown lines two metres inside each baseline mark the deep zone for cross-court balls. A two-metre lane along the singles sideline on each player's down-the-line side, marked with cones at the service line and the baseline, is the only target for down-the-line balls. Basket at the net post.
instructions: Rally cross-court with heavy topspin; every cross-court ball must land in the deep zone.
Either player may go down the line at any time, but that ball must be flat and land in the sideline lane.
The point goes live the moment someone goes down the line.
First to ten, alternating who starts from the basket.
Second game: the down-the-line ball is allowed only off a ball that landed short of the deep zone.
coaching_points: Cross-court: fast racket head from low to high with a high finish; make it heavy, not hard.
Down the line: flatten the swing path and finish forward at shoulder height.
Take the line ball early and inside the baseline; from behind the baseline the line is a low-percentage shot.
After going down the line, recover to the centre mark and split; the reply comes back fast.
progressions: Shrink the lane to one metre.
Cross-court balls must also clear the net by two racket lengths.
Play points from a serve.
regressions: Widen the lane to three metres.
Cooperate through the first down-the-line ball before the point goes live.
Move the deep zone line to three metres inside the baseline.

name: Ball Machine Random: Split Step on Every Release
summary: Uses a random-oscillating machine to enforce a split step on every ball and a balanced base for every contact.
setup: Ball machine on the far baseline at the centre, random oscillation, fast pace with topspin, three-second interval. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target. A second player, if present, stands behind the near baseline and counts the split steps that land before the ball crosses the net.
instructions: Hitter split-steps as the machine releases each ball, then moves to it and hits deep.
Every ball must be played from a balanced base: no hitting while still running.
Sets of ten balls; score one for each deep ball hit from a set position, zero for a deep ball hit on the run.
Four sets with a minute between; recover to the centre mark after every ball.
Last set: every ball cross-court.
coaching_points: The split lands as the ball leaves the machine, not when it bounces.
First step is explosive, the last two are small so you arrive balanced.
Hit heavy and high when you arrive late; flat only when you are early and set.
Recover before the ball has landed: the next release is three seconds away.
progressions: Shorten the interval to two seconds.
Widen the machine's oscillation to full width.
Any ball landing inside the service line must be attacked down the line.
regressions: Slow the interval to five seconds.
Set the machine to alternate sides instead of random.
Score every deep ball whether set or not.

name: Backhand Drop Shot off the Short Ball
summary: Builds a disguised backhand drop shot into hoop targets just over the net, played off a short feed and followed in.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket. Hitter on the near baseline on the ad side. Two hoops on the far side a metre from the net: one a metre inside the far singles sideline on the cross-court side and one on the centre line. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder hits a ball that lands a metre inside the near service line on the backhand side.
Hitter moves in and plays a backhand drop shot into either hoop.
Score two for a hoop, one for a ball that bounces twice inside the far service box, zero otherwise.
Ten balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates a deep ball, which must be driven, and a short ball, which must be dropped.
coaching_points: Show the drive: same shoulder turn and take-back, then open the face late.
Soft hands: hold the racket loosely and let the ball drop onto the strings.
Cut under and slightly across so the ball checks and stays low.
Follow the drop shot forward two steps; a good drop still comes back.
progressions: Remove the centre hoop and use only the wide one.
Feeder follows the drop shot with a lob that must be dealt with.
The drop must be hit from behind the service line.
regressions: Replace the hoops with the whole far service box as the target.
Feeder tosses the short ball underarm.
Hitter starts at the service line.

name: Five-Ball Pattern: Cross, Cross, Line, Cross, Finish
summary: Runs a fixed five-ball shot pattern with full recovery between balls so direction changes become automatic under fatigue.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. Cones mark the targets on the far side: a cone two metres inside each far corner for the deep balls, and a cone in the middle of each far service box for the finishing ball. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder plays five balls in sequence: forehand side, forehand side, backhand side, backhand side, then a short ball to the middle.
Hitter answers with the pattern: cross-court, cross-court, down the line, cross-court, then a finish at either service-box cone.
Every ball is hit with full recovery to the centre mark between shots.
Five balls, then rotate; score one per target hit, three for the finish.
Second round: the feeder reverses the pattern so it starts on the backhand.
coaching_points: Know the next shot before this one is hit; the pattern is decided, the movement is not.
The line ball is the change: contact later and drive flat; the others are heavy and high.
Recover to the centre mark, not to where the last ball came from.
On the finish, move forward through contact and land inside the court.
progressions: Feeder speeds the interval so the fifth ball arrives as the hitter recovers.
Shrink the corner targets to one-metre cone squares.
Hitter calls a new pattern before each set with the line ball in a different position.
regressions: Three balls only: cross, line, finish.
Feeder tosses underarm from the far service line.
Widen all targets to the whole far half.

name: Throw the Serve: Overarm Throws into the Box
summary: Builds the serving action without a racket by throwing balls overarm into the diagonal service box from a side-on stance.
setup: Players stand on the near service line, one on each side of the centre line, with a basket of red or orange balls between them. A hoop in the middle of each far service box. No rackets: this is an overarm throw with the serving action, side-on, ball in the throwing hand.
instructions: Stand side-on with the front foot pointing at the far net post and the ball held above the head.
Throw overarm over the net into the diagonal service box, aiming for the hoop.
Score one for the box, three for the hoop; ten throws each, then swap sides so the other box is the target.
Round two: hold a racket in the other hand and lift it up before the throw so both arms move together.
Round three: throw from two metres behind the service line.
coaching_points: Elbow up and back before the throw, hand by the ear.
Throw up and over, not down; the ball goes over the net before it comes down.
Front foot stays planted; the back hip turns through towards the target.
Finish with the throwing hand down past the opposite knee.
progressions: Throw from two metres behind the service line.
Replace the hoop with a single cone that must be hit.
Hold the racket up in the free hand as if tossing while you throw.
regressions: Throw from a metre in front of the service line.
Widen the target to the whole far half.
Throw to a partner's hands across the net instead of into the box.

name: Toss and Catch on the Spot
summary: Fixes the service toss by tossing into a hoop on the ground and catching at full stretch without moving the feet.
setup: Each player stands a metre behind the near service line with a hoop on the ground a racket length in front of the front foot and slightly to the racket side; that is where a good toss would land. Racket in the hitting hand held up in the trophy position. Basket of balls beside each player.
instructions: Toss the ball from the fingertips, arm straight, releasing at eye height, and let it drop without moving the feet.
A ball that lands in the hoop scores; ten tosses, count the score.
Next ten: toss and catch the ball at full stretch with the tossing arm, without the feet moving.
Next ten: toss, and let the racket reach up to touch the ball at the top of the toss without hitting it.
Finish with five tosses followed by a full swing that hits the ball into the far box.
coaching_points: Ball on the fingertips, not in the palm; the palm throws it crooked.
Lift the arm straight up like lifting a tray; release when the hand reaches eye height.
Toss only as high as the racket can reach at full stretch.
Feet still: if you have to move to catch it, the toss was wrong.
progressions: Shrink the target from a hoop to a single cone the ball must land on.
Toss with the eyes closed for the catch round.
Toss from behind the baseline with the same hoop distance.
regressions: Use a two-metre cone square instead of a hoop.
Toss with a red ball, which is lighter and slower.
Toss and catch only, no racket, until eight out of ten land in the hoop.

name: Service-Line Serve into the Big Box
summary: First real serves from the service line, scoring every ball that lands in the diagonal box before stepping back.
setup: Servers stand on the near service line, a metre either side of the centre line, serving diagonally into the far service boxes. A cone on each far singles sideline at the service line and one on the far centre line at the service line make the boxes easy to see. Basket between the servers. Two serve at a time; anyone else collects behind the far baseline and swaps in every ten serves.
instructions: Serve overarm from the service line into the diagonal box; underarm serves count for the first ten if needed.
Score one for every serve in the box; ten serves, then swap sides so the other box is served.
Round two: only overarm serves count.
Round three: serve from two steps behind the service line.
Keep a running total per player; the target is seven out of ten before moving back.
coaching_points: Toss slightly in front so the body moves forward into the serve.
Reach up: contact at the highest point the arm can reach.
Swing the racket up and over the ball, finishing across the body.
Front foot points at the net post and stays still until the ball is hit.
progressions: Serve from halfway between the service line and the baseline.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
Score only serves that land past the middle of the box.
regressions: Serve from a metre inside the service line.
Allow the ball to bounce once before serving, a drop-hit serve.
Use a red ball.

name: Return Catch: Track, Trap, Then Hit
summary: Introduces the return by tracking a gentle serve and trapping it on the strings before progressing to a blocked return.
setup: Server on the far service line at the centre with the basket, serving gently overarm into the near deuce box. Returner on the near service line in the middle of the deuce box, racket held out in front with two hands in a ready position. Nothing else on court.
instructions: Server hits an easy serve into the box.
Returner moves to the ball and traps it on the racket strings after one bounce, letting it roll to a stop, no swing.
Five traps, then five returns where the returner blocks the ball back over the net to the server.
Swap roles after each ten.
Round two: the returner calls 'forehand' or 'backhand' as the ball leaves the server's racket, then traps or returns.
coaching_points: Split step as the server hits, then move to the ball with the racket already out in front.
Track the ball all the way onto the strings; the trap is a soft catch, not a hit.
Turn the shoulders as soon as you know the side.
For the block, short swing, firm wrist, aim back at the server.
progressions: Server serves from two metres behind the service line.
Returner must return every serve, no traps.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Server tosses underarm instead of serving.
Returner catches the ball in the free hand before trapping with the racket.
Use a red ball.

name: Serve and Return Points in the Boxes
summary: Plays live points from a service-line serve inside the four service boxes, so beginners learn the serve-return exchange at a slow pace.
setup: One player on each side. The server stands on the service line and serves diagonally into the far box; the returner stands on their service line in that box. Cones on the singles sidelines and centre lines at both service lines mark the playing area: the two boxes on each side. Basket at the net post. Serve changes hands every two points.
instructions: Server serves overarm from the service line into the diagonal box; one serve, with an underarm second serve allowed.
Returner returns into any box and the point is played inside the boxes.
First to seven, then change ends and change the serving box.
A serve that misses the box twice loses the point.
Third game: the return must go cross-court, back to the server's box.
coaching_points: Server: toss in front and hit up; the box is close, so height wins.
Returner: split step on the server's contact, racket out in front.
Short swings for both: the boxes are small and the ball is slow.
After the serve, take one step in and get ready; the return comes back quickly.
progressions: Serve from two metres behind the service line.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
The return must be hit before the second bounce, no trapping.
regressions: Serve underarm for the whole game.
Allow two bounces on the return.
Use a red ball.

name: Step-Back Serve Ladder
summary: Moves the server back one cone at a time from the service line to the baseline, earning each step with serves in the box.
setup: Server starts beside the near service line on the deuce side, serving into the far deuce box. Four cones mark serving spots in a straight line back towards the baseline: on the service line, two metres back, four metres back, and on the baseline. Basket beside the first cone. Extra players collect behind the far baseline and swap in after each set of five.
instructions: Serve from the first cone until three serves out of five land in the box.
Move back one cone and repeat; a failed set of five means you stay on that cone.
The ladder is complete when three of five go in from the baseline.
Swap in the next player after every set of five.
Second time up the ladder, serve into the ad box.
coaching_points: The swing does not change as you move back; the toss goes a little more in front.
Reach up at contact from every spot; hitting higher adds length, hitting harder does not.
Land on the front foot inside the court after the serve.
Same routine before every serve: bounce, breathe, toss.
progressions: Require four out of five at each cone.
Add a fifth cone a metre behind the baseline.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Require two out of five at each cone.
Remove the baseline cone so the ladder ends four metres back.
Use an orange ball.

name: Return Ready: Split on the Toss
summary: Times the returner's split step to the server's toss and contact, then returns cross-court past the service line.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, tossing a ball up and hitting an easy serve-like feed into the near deuce box. Returner on the near baseline on the deuce side, a metre inside the singles sideline. A throwdown one metre in front of the returner marks where the split step should land. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses the ball up like a serve; the returner split-steps as the toss goes up and lands as the feeder makes contact.
Feeder hits the ball into the box; returner moves and returns it cross-court over the net.
Score one for a return that lands past the far service line.
Eight returns, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder sometimes catches the toss instead of hitting; a returner who has already run forward loses a point.
coaching_points: Feet leave the ground as the toss goes up, land as the racket hits the ball.
Land on the balls of the feet with the knees bent, ready to push either way.
Racket out in front at waist height, both hands on it.
First step is towards the ball, not backwards.
progressions: Feeder serves properly from the far baseline.
Feeder serves to either box; the returner must cover both.
Returner must return down the middle past a cone on the far centre line.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm and the returner splits on the release.
Returner catches the ball in the free hand after the split, then returns the next one.
Use an orange ball.

name: Serve Target Bingo: Four Quarters
summary: Turns serve placement into bingo by splitting the box into four quarters that each have to be hit once.
setup: Server stands halfway between the near service line and the baseline, on the deuce side, serving into the far deuce box. Four cones split that box into quarters: one in the centre of the box, one on the far service line directly behind it, and one on each side line of the box level with the centre cone. Basket beside the server. With more than one server, share the basket and take turns serving five each.
instructions: Serve five balls, calling which quarter you are aiming for before each toss.
Tick off a quarter when a serve lands in it; bingo is all four quarters ticked.
First to bingo wins the round; with one player, count the serves needed.
Round two from two steps further back.
Round three into the ad box.
coaching_points: Pick the quarter, then look at the toss; do not look at the target during the swing.
Front quarters: hit up more and softer; back quarters: reach and hit through.
Wide quarters: toss slightly further to the racket side; middle quarters: toss straight up.
Same rhythm every serve: bounce, toss, hit.
progressions: Serve from the baseline.
Bingo requires the quarters in a set order.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Serve from the service line.
Split the box into two halves instead of four quarters.
Use an orange ball.

name: Spin Serve: High Over the Net and Dip In
summary: Introduces the spin second serve by making every serve clear a raised racket at the net post and still land in the box.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket, serving into the far deuce box. A partner stands at the near net post holding a racket straight up in the air: the serve must clear the net by that racket's length. The whole far box is the target, no cones. Extra players collect behind the far baseline and swap in every ten serves.
instructions: Hold the racket with the continental grip so the edge leads up to the ball.
Toss slightly behind the head and brush up the back of the ball, aiming to clear the raised racket at the net post.
Score one for a serve that clears the racket and lands in the box; zero for a serve that goes in but does not clear it.
Ten serves, then swap with the racket-holder.
Second round: the racket-holder calls 'kick' when the ball bounces higher than their waist on the far side.
coaching_points: Edge first: the strings face the side fence at the top of the swing, not the net.
Brush up the back of the ball; the racket goes up more than forward.
Toss a little behind the head so the racket can come up under the ball.
Finish with the racket on the hitting-arm side of the body, not across it.
progressions: The serve must clear two racket lengths above the net.
Serve into the ad box, where the spin takes the ball away from a right-handed returner.
Add a returner who must return the kick above waist height.
regressions: Serve from the service line.
The serve must clear the net by a racket head, not a whole racket.
Use a green ball.

name: Serve Countdown: Twenty to Zero
summary: Builds serving consistency under a running count where every serve in takes one off and every miss adds one back.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side, serving into the far deuce box, with the basket beside them. No targets. With two to four players, everyone serves in turn from the same side, one serve each, and each player keeps their own count.
instructions: Start at twenty; every serve in the box takes one off the count.
Every miss adds one back on.
Serve alternately into the deuce and ad boxes, switching sides after each serve.
The set ends at zero; note how many serves it took.
Second set with second serves only: no first-serve pace, spin on every ball.
coaching_points: Treat every serve as the first one: same routine, same toss, no rush after a miss.
When a serve misses long, toss slightly more in front on the next one.
When a serve hits the net, reach higher and hit up through the ball.
Breathe out as the racket drops behind the back.
progressions: Start the countdown at thirty instead of twenty.
Only serves that land past the middle of the box count.
A miss adds two.
regressions: Start the countdown at ten instead of twenty.
Misses add nothing back onto the count.
Serve from two metres inside the baseline.

name: Return Block: Short Swing off a Fast Feed
summary: Teaches the blocked return by feeding fast flat balls at the returner, who must send them back deep with almost no backswing.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting fast flat feeds with the racket at the returner, alternating forehand and backhand sides. Returner on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the depth target. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a fast ball at the returner's forehand or backhand.
Returner blocks it back with a short swing, aiming past the far throwdown line down the middle.
Score one for a deep return; count out of ten.
Ten balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder does not say which side; the returner must read it.
coaching_points: Racket back only to the hip; the ball's pace does the work.
Contact out in front with a firm wrist and a short follow-through towards the target.
Split step as the feeder's racket meets the ball.
Step into the ball with the front foot; do not lean back.
progressions: Feeder serves from the far baseline instead of feeding.
Returner starts a metre inside the baseline.
Returns must go cross-court instead of down the middle.
regressions: Feeder feeds at three-quarter pace.
Feeder calls the side before each feed.
Widen the target to anywhere past the far service line.

name: Serve and Return: The Return Must Cross the Service Line
summary: Scores the serve-return exchange on one thing only, return depth, so returners learn to lift the ball past the service line.
setup: Server behind the near baseline and returner behind the far baseline, both on the deuce side. Throwdowns along the near service line make the depth line obvious to the returner. Basket beside the server. Two serves per point, then the ball is dead after the return: no rally.
instructions: Server serves; the returner returns anywhere in the court.
The return scores a point only if it lands past the near service line.
A missed or short return scores for the server; a double fault scores for the returner.
Ten points, then swap roles and boxes.
Second game: the return must also land cross-court.
coaching_points: Returner: aim two racket lengths over the net; depth on the return comes from height.
Returner: short backswing on first serves, full swing on second serves.
Server: land inside the court and get ready; a short return is your point.
Both: split step on the other player's contact.
progressions: The return must land within two metres of the baseline.
Play the point out after a deep return.
Server may serve to either box.
regressions: Server serves from two metres inside the baseline.
Serve second serves only, no first serves.
Any return over the net scores.

name: Serve, Land, Split on the Throwdown
summary: Trains what happens after the serve: land inside the court, two quick steps, and a split step on a throwdown before the ball bounces.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. A throwdown a metre inside the baseline, in line with the centre mark, marks where the split step after the serve should land. No targets in the box. A partner stands behind the server and calls 'late' if the split lands after the serve bounces; extra players wait behind the partner and swap in every ten serves.
instructions: Serve into the deuce box, land on the front foot inside the court, and take two quick steps to split on the throwdown.
The split must be on the ground before the serve bounces on the far side; the partner calls 'late' if not.
Score one for a serve in plus a split in time.
Ten serves, then serve from the ad side with the throwdown moved to the other side of the centre mark.
Last five: the partner rolls a ball towards either corner after the split and the server moves to it.
coaching_points: Land inside the baseline on the front foot with the back leg kicking up behind.
First step out of the landing is forward and across, not sideways.
Split with the feet wider than the shoulders, weight on the balls of the feet.
Eyes on the far side as you split, not on your own serve.
progressions: Move the throwdown two metres inside the baseline.
Partner hits a real return that the server must play after the split.
Serve from the ad side and split to the deuce side of the mark.
regressions: Split anywhere inside the baseline, no throwdown.
Serve from the service line so there is more time.
Serve at half pace so there is more time to land and split.

name: Return Direction: Cross-Court Deep or Down the Middle
summary: Alternates two return targets, the cross-court corner and the deep middle, so the returner learns to choose direction with the contact point.
setup: Server behind the far baseline on the deuce side with the basket, serving into the near deuce box. Returner behind the near baseline on the deuce side. Two targets on the far side: a two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner (the returner's forehand cross-court corner) and a two-metre cone box on the far baseline straddling the centre mark.
instructions: Server serves at three-quarter pace into the box.
Returner alternates targets: one return cross-court into the corner box, the next down the middle into the centre box.
Score two for a box, one for a return past the far service line on the correct side, zero otherwise.
Ten returns, then swap roles.
Second round: the server calls the target as they toss.
coaching_points: Cross-court: contact further in front and let the hips open to the corner.
Middle: contact level with the front hip and drive straight through the ball.
Same short backswing for both; the direction comes from the contact point.
Recover to the centre mark after every return.
progressions: Shrink the boxes to one metre.
Server serves at full pace.
Server calls the target as the ball is struck, not on the toss.
regressions: Server serves from the service line.
Widen the targets to the whole far half.
Returner chooses the target and calls it before the serve.

name: Serve Plus One: Forehand to the Deep Target
summary: Links the serve to the first groundstroke by having the returner block cross-court and the server hit a deep forehand behind it.
