setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. Partner behind the far baseline on the deuce side as the returner, returning every serve cross-court at rally pace. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline marks the deep target for the server's second shot. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline and swap in as the returner every ten points.
instructions: Server serves; the returner blocks it back cross-court to the server's forehand side.
Server recovers and hits a forehand deep past the far throwdown line; the ball is then dead.
Score one for a serve in, one for the plus-one deep, two extra if it lands in the corner.
Ten sequences, then rotate roles.
Second round: the returner returns down the middle so the server must move round to the forehand.
coaching_points: Land and split before the return is struck; the plus-one starts with the feet.
Aim the plus-one high and heavy to the deep target; a rushed flat ball lands short.
Recover to the centre mark after the serve, not to where you served from.
If the return is short, move in and take it early; do not wait for it.
progressions: The returner returns anywhere, not only cross-court.
The plus-one must be an inside-out forehand from the backhand corner.
Play the point out after the plus-one.
regressions: Returner hand-feeds the return instead of returning a live serve.
Widen the deep target to anywhere past the far service line.
Serve from two metres inside the baseline.

name: Second Serves Only Points
summary: Plays full points where the server gets a single second serve, so the spin serve is trusted under real pressure.
setup: One player each side of the net behind the baselines, playing full-court singles points on the singles court. Basket at the net post. The only change from a normal point: the server gets one serve, and it must be a spin second serve, so a miss is a double fault. With three or four players, rotate in after every four points.
instructions: Server has one serve; a miss is a double fault.
Play the point out normally.
Games to seven points, then swap server.
Serve into the deuce and ad boxes alternately as in a match.
Third game: the returner must attack every serve and get to the net behind it.
coaching_points: Spin the ball in: the second serve has margin over the net and drops in from height.
Toss slightly behind the head so the racket brushes up the back of the ball.
Same routine under pressure: bounce, breathe, toss.
Returner: step in and take the second serve early, before it kicks up.
progressions: The serve must land past the middle of the box.
Returner starts a metre inside the baseline.
Serve only into the ad box, where a right-hander's kick pulls the returner wide.
regressions: Allow one first serve every other point.
Serve from a metre inside the baseline.
Points are replayed after a double fault instead of lost.

name: Slice Serve Wide: Past the Cone
summary: Develops the wide slice serve in the deuce court, scored on whether the ball curves past a cone outside the sideline after the bounce.
setup: Server behind the near baseline, a metre to the right of the centre mark, serving into the far deuce box. A cone on the far singles sideline a metre inside the service line marks the wide target; a second cone a metre outside the far singles sideline, level with the service line, marks where the ball should pass after the bounce. Basket beside the server. Resting players collect behind the far baseline and call whether the ball curved past the outside cone.
instructions: Toss slightly to the right and in front; hit the outside of the ball, brushing across it from left to right.
Serve wide: the ball should land inside the cone on the sideline and curve past the outside cone after the bounce.
Score one for the box, two for wide of the inside cone, three if the caller says it passed the outside cone.
Ten serves, then rotate.
Second round: alternate the wide slice with a serve down the T from the same toss.
coaching_points: Contact the right side of the ball at three o'clock; the strings cut across it, not through it.
Toss a little further right than for the flat serve so the swing can go across the ball.
Keep the swing speed up; a slow slice floats and sits up.
Finish across the body with the racket ending by the left hip.
progressions: Move the inside cone half a metre closer to the sideline.
Add a returner who must return the wide serve cross-court.
Serve the slice into the ad box, where it curves into the returner's body.
regressions: Serve from two metres inside the baseline.
Widen the target to the outside half of the box.
Use a green ball so the curve is easier to see.

name: Return Neutraliser: Deep Middle off the Kick Serve
summary: Trains the safe return against a kick serve, taken high or early and sent deep down the middle to take away the server's angles.
setup: Server behind the far baseline with the basket, serving kick serves into the near boxes. Returner behind the near baseline. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline, with a throwdown two metres either side of the centre mark on it, marks the deep-middle target: a four-metre-wide box against the far baseline.
instructions: Server serves kick serves, alternating boxes.
Returner returns every serve deep down the middle into the throwdown box, taking the ball at shoulder height or above.
Score two for the box, one for anywhere past the throwdown line, zero for short.
Ten returns, then swap roles.
Second round: the returner steps in a metre and takes the serve on the rise before it kicks.
coaching_points: Take the ball early or high, not in between: on the rise inside the baseline, or at the top of the kick from behind it.
Aim high over the middle of the net; the deep middle gives the server no angle.
Short backswing with a long finish towards the target.
Split as the server's racket hits the ball, then move forward, never backward.
progressions: Shrink the middle box to two metres.
Server serves at full pace.
Play the point out after a return into the box.
regressions: Server serves second-serve pace with less kick.
Widen the target to anywhere past the throwdown line.
Server serves from a metre inside the baseline.

name: Same Toss, Three Serves
summary: Builds serve disguise by hitting flat, slice and kick serves from one toss while a partner tries to call the serve before contact.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. A partner stands behind the far baseline in the returner's position and, on each serve, calls 'flat', 'slice' or 'kick' as early as they can read it from the toss and swing. Extra players wait behind the server and count how many calls came before contact.
instructions: Server hits flat, slice and kick serves in any order, all from as close to one toss position as possible.
Partner calls the serve type as soon as they think they know; the counter notes whether the call came before or after contact.
Score one for every serve in the box where the call came after contact or was wrong.
Ten serves, then rotate roles.
Second round: the server calls the serve out loud before the toss and works only on keeping the toss identical.
coaching_points: One toss: slightly in front and to the right, high enough for the kick; adapt the swing, not the toss.
Flat: hit through the back of the ball; slice: across it; kick: up the back and over the top.
Same routine, same rhythm, same shoulder turn for all three.
Keep the toss arm up through contact on every serve so the arm gives nothing away.
progressions: Partner must call before the toss reaches its peak.
Add a fourth option: the body serve.
Partner returns the serve after calling it.
regressions: Two serves only: flat and slice.
Serve from a metre inside the baseline.
Partner calls only after the bounce, and the score is simply serves in.

name: Return on the Rise from Inside the Baseline
summary: Moves the returner inside the baseline and rewards taking the serve on the rise with a compact swing and a deep return.
setup: Server behind the far baseline with the basket, serving first serves at three-quarter pace into the near deuce box. Returner starts one metre inside the near baseline on the deuce side, on a throwdown. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the depth target. Nothing else on court.
instructions: Server serves; the returner takes the ball on the rise from inside the baseline and returns deep past the throwdown line.
Score two for a return past the line, one for a return in play, minus one for stepping back behind the baseline.
Ten returns, then swap roles.
Second round from the ad side.
Third round: the server mixes first and second serves; the returner must hold the position for both.
coaching_points: Compact swing: racket back to the hip and through; the ball is rising into the strings.
Contact well in front and lean into the ball; a late contact on the rise flies long.
Split as the ball leaves the racket and take the first step forward, not sideways.
Keep the head still and the eyes level; the ball is coming faster than it looks.
progressions: Start two metres inside the baseline.
Server serves at full pace.
Returns must go cross-court into the far corner.
regressions: Start on the baseline instead of inside it.
Server serves second serves only.
Score any return in play.

name: Serve Percentage Sets: Play the Score
summary: Serves whole games with the score called out loud, so first-serve percentage is measured where it matters.
setup: Server behind the near baseline with the basket, serving a game's worth of points into alternating boxes as in a match: deuce box, ad box, deuce box, and so on. No returner; resting players stand behind the far baseline and call each serve in or out. Nothing else on court.
instructions: Serve a game: call the score out loud before each point, starting at love-all.
A first serve in wins the point; a first serve out means a second serve, which must go in or the point is lost.
Play to game, then note first-serve percentage over the points played.
Serve four games, alternating who serves when there is more than one player.
Last game: a first serve must land past the middle of the box to count.
coaching_points: Pick the target before the bounce and commit; changing your mind mid-toss is a miss.
Second serve: more spin, more height, same swing speed.
At 30-40 or deuce, slow the routine down, not the swing.
Land inside the court and get ready even with no returner; the habit is the point.
progressions: First serves must land in the outside half of the box to count as in.
Add a returner who plays the point out.
Serve a whole set of games, tracking percentage per game.
regressions: Serve from a metre inside the baseline.
Second serves are not scored; a first serve out simply replays the point.
Play games to three points.

name: Return Anticipation: Read the Toss
summary: Trains the returner to read the serve from the toss and the swing, calling wide, T or body before contact and then returning.
setup: Server behind the far baseline with the basket, serving into the near deuce box with three serves: wide slice, flat down the T, and a kick into the body. Returner behind the near baseline on the deuce side. No targets: the score is about the call.
instructions: Server serves any of the three serves without warning.
Returner calls 'wide', 'T' or 'body' before the server makes contact, reading the toss and the swing, then returns the serve.
Score one for a correct call, one for a return in play, three for both.
Ten serves, then swap roles.
Second round from the ad box.
coaching_points: Watch the toss: further right usually means slice, further behind the head means kick.
Call early and commit; a late call is worth nothing.
Even when the call is wrong, split on contact and play the ball; the split covers the mistake.
First step is towards the called serve; adjust with the second step if you were wrong.
progressions: Server disguises the toss so all three serves come from one toss position.
The call must come before the toss reaches its peak.
Play the point out after the return.
regressions: Server uses two serves only: wide and T.
Server tells the returner the pattern for the first five serves.
Server serves at three-quarter pace.

name: Serve and Recover: The Two-Ball Serve
summary: Puts a real second ball behind the serve, fed deep to the backhand corner as the serve is struck, so landing and recovery are trained under time pressure.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. Feeder stands beside the near net post on the server's left with a second basket, ready to feed a deep ball into the server's backhand corner the moment the serve is struck. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target for the second ball. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Server serves into the deuce box.
As the serve is struck the feeder hits a deep ball into the server's backhand corner.
Server lands, recovers and hits the second ball deep past the throwdown line.
Score one for the serve in, two for the second ball deep.
Ten sequences, then rotate: server to feeder, feeder to the queue.
coaching_points: Land on the front foot and push off it immediately; there is no time to watch the serve.
Split as the feeder makes contact, then a crossover step to the backhand corner.
Hit the second ball high and heavy: recovering the position matters more than pace.
Recover to the centre mark after the second ball as if a third ball were coming.
progressions: Feeder feeds to either corner without warning.
Feeder feeds short so the second ball must be attacked.
Add a third ball after the recovery.
regressions: Feeder waits until the server has landed before feeding.
Feeder feeds to the forehand side.
Widen the target to anywhere past the far service line.

name: Serve Under Fatigue: Ten After the Shuttle
summary: Tests the serve routine when tired by serving ten balls straight after baseline-to-net shuttle runs and comparing the score with a fresh set.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. A cone at the near net on the centre line and a cone on the near baseline at the centre mark mark the shuttle run: baseline to net and back, twice. Resting players collect behind the far baseline and call serves in or out.
instructions: Serve a fresh set of ten first, alternating deuce and ad boxes, and note the score.
Run the shuttle: baseline cone to net cone and back, twice, at full speed.
Immediately serve ten balls, alternating boxes, using the full routine before each serve; score serves in.
Three rounds with a two-minute rest between; the aim is the same score tired as fresh.
Last round: second serves only.
coaching_points: Breathe out fully twice before the first toss; the heart rate drops faster than you think.
Slow the routine down when tired: bounce, bounce, breathe, toss.
Legs still bend and drive; tired legs make the arm do the work and the toss drifts.
Toss height stays the same; do not shorten the toss to get the serve over with.
progressions: Three shuttle runs instead of two.
Serve only five balls after each shuttle so the fatigue is fresher on every serve.
First serves must land past the middle of the box.
regressions: Run one shuttle instead of two.
Rest thirty seconds before serving.
Serve into either box, no alternation.

name: Serve Patterns by Score: The 30-30 Plan
summary: Makes the server commit to a written serve plan for pressure scores and execute it against called scores.
setup: Server behind the near baseline with the basket. Cones mark three targets in each far box: T, body and wide. A resting player, or the server alone, calls a score before each serve (15-30, 30-30, 40-30, deuce, ad-out) and the server serves the plan written for that score: first serve to the planned target, second serve to the body. Nothing else on court.
instructions: Before starting, write a plan: which first-serve target for each of the five scores.
Caller announces a score; server serves the planned first serve, and if it misses, a second serve to the body.
Score two for the planned target, one for the box, minus one for a double fault.
Twenty points, then swap roles.
Second round: on 30-30 and deuce the caller may say 'change' as the server tosses, and the server must switch to the T.
coaching_points: Decide the target before the bounce; at 30-30 the decision is the pressure, not the serve.
Second serve to the body: kick into the hip with high margin.
Same tempo at every score; the routine is the thing that never changes.
Toss position stays identical for every target; only the swing path changes.
progressions: Shrink the targets to one-metre cone squares.
The caller adds break points, where the first serve must go wide.
Add a returner and play the point out at deuce and ad-out.
regressions: Two scores only: 30-30 and deuce.
Second serves may go anywhere in the box.
Serve from a metre inside the baseline.

name: Return Plus One: Take the Middle
summary: Links a deep-middle return to an aggressive second ball, so the returner neutralises first and attacks the short reply.
setup: Server behind the far baseline with the basket, serving first serves. Returner behind the near baseline. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline, with a throwdown two metres either side of the centre mark on it, marks the deep-middle box. The server plays the point out after the return.
instructions: Server serves; the returner returns deep into the middle box.
The server's next ball is live; the returner takes the first short ball and attacks it to the open side.
Play the point out; the returner scores two for a point won after a middle return, the server one for any point won.
Ten points, then swap roles.
Second round: the returner must attack the second ball down the line.
coaching_points: The deep middle return takes away the server's angle; the plus-one is where you attack.
After the return, move forward a metre and split; expect the short ball.
Hit the plus-one early, on the rise, to the side the server has left.
If the server's ball is deep, reset with another deep middle ball; do not force it.
progressions: Shrink the middle box to two metres.
Server serves second serves only and the returner must attack the return itself.
Returner must finish the point at the net.
regressions: Server serves at three-quarter pace.
Any return past the throwdown line counts as the middle.
Cooperate until the plus-one, then play the point out.

name: Serve Wide, First Ball into the Open Court
summary: Drills the classic deuce-court pattern: a wide serve that drags the returner out, then the first ball into the space it leaves.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. Returner behind the far baseline on the deuce side. A cone on the far singles sideline a metre inside the service line marks the wide serve target; a two-metre cone box in the far ad corner, the open court after a wide deuce serve, marks the first-ball target. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline and swap in as the returner.
instructions: Server serves wide to the cone; the returner returns cross-court or down the middle, whichever they can manage.
Server hits the first ball into the open-court cone box.
Score one for the wide serve, two for the first ball in the box; the ball is dead after the first ball.
Ten sequences, then rotate roles.
Second round: play the point out after the first ball.
coaching_points: The wide serve opens the court; the first ball goes where the returner is not, not where you like hitting.
Land, split, and move to the ball as the return is struck; the open court closes fast.
First ball: heavy and deep is enough, a winner is a bonus.
If the return comes back wide, hit behind the returner instead; they are already running.
progressions: Shrink the cone box to one metre.
The returner may return anywhere, including down the line.
Add the ad-court version: kick serve wide, first ball into the deuce corner.
regressions: Returner hand-feeds the return to the server's forehand.
Widen the open-court target to the whole far ad half.
Serve from a metre inside the baseline.

name: Chip Return Short Cross-Court Against Serve and Volley
summary: Trains the low chipped return that makes a serve-and-volleyer volley up from below the net, played out as live points.
setup: Server behind the far baseline with the basket, serving and following every serve to the net. Returner behind the near baseline on the deuce side. A hoop on the far side a metre inside the far singles sideline and a metre behind the net, on the cross-court side, marks the low chip target at the incoming volleyer's feet.
instructions: Server serves and volleys on every point.
Returner chips the return short and low cross-court towards the hoop so the volleyer must volley up from below the net.
Play the point out; the returner scores two if the point is won after a chip into the hoop area, the server one for any point won.
Ten points, then swap roles.
Second round from the ad side.
coaching_points: Continental grip, short backswing and a slightly open face: the ball should skid, not float.
Take the ball early and in front so it dips at the volleyer's feet.
Follow the chip in a step or two; a dipping ball often comes back short.
If the serve is a kick, block flat instead of chipping; a chipped high ball sits up.
progressions: Move the hoop half a metre closer to the sideline.
Server serves at full pace.
Returner must follow the chip to the net.
regressions: Server serves at three-quarter pace and stops at the service line.
Replace the hoop with the whole far service box.
Server hand-feeds from the service line and then closes in.

name: Kick Serve Bounce Height Check
summary: Measures the kick serve by the height the ball passes a partner standing at the far baseline, not by where it lands.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the ad side with the basket, serving kick serves into the far ad box. A partner stands behind the far baseline in the returner's position on a cone that marks the spot. Resting players collect behind them. No targets in the box: the score is the bounce height at the partner.
instructions: Serve kick serves into the ad box; the partner stands still and lets each ball bounce past them without playing it.
Partner calls the height the ball passes them: 'waist', 'chest' or 'shoulder'.
Score one for waist, two for chest, three for shoulder; only serves in the box count.
Ten serves, then swap roles.
Second round: the partner returns the serve from above shoulder height, and nothing else counts.
coaching_points: Toss behind the head and to the left, then swing up the back of the ball from seven to one o'clock.
Legs drive up into the ball; the kick comes from the upward path, not the wrist alone.
Contact slightly behind the head; a toss in front makes a slice, not a kick.
Finish on the racket-arm side with the racket pointing down; do not pull across the body.
progressions: Only chest and shoulder height count.
Partner stands a metre inside the baseline so the ball must kick sooner.
Serve the kick wide in the ad box past a cone on the sideline.
regressions: Serve from a metre inside the baseline.
Score any serve in the box, plus one if it passes above waist height.
Use a green ball to feel the brush before switching back.

name: Return Stance Switch: Blocked Backhand, Full Forehand
summary: Teaches the returner to match the swing to the serve, blocking fast first serves and driving slower second serves.
setup: Server behind the far baseline with the basket, mixing first serves to the backhand and second serves to the forehand in any order. Returner behind the near baseline on the deuce side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the depth target for both returns.
instructions: Server serves; the returner reads the serve and chooses the reply: a compact block on a first serve to the backhand, or a full-swing drive on a second serve to the forehand.
Both returns must land past the throwdown line.
Score one for a deep return, one more if the swing matched the serve, minus one for a full swing at a first serve.
Ten returns, then swap roles.
Second round from the ad side, where the block is on the forehand and the drive on the backhand.
coaching_points: First serve: racket back to the hip only, contact in front, hold the finish short.
Second serve: full unit turn, step in, and swing through the ball above the shoulder.
Decide from the toss and the speed of the swing, not after the bounce.
Split step on contact for both; the difference is the backswing, not the footwork.
progressions: Server serves any serve to any side and the returner must match the reply to the pace.
Blocked returns must go cross-court and driven returns down the line.
Play the point out after the return.
regressions: Server calls 'first' or 'second' before the toss.
Server serves at three-quarter pace on both serves.
Score any return in play.

name: Serve Speed Change: Three Speeds, Same Spot
summary: Develops control of serve pace by hitting the same target at three speeds with an unchanged swing shape.
setup: Server behind the near baseline on the deuce side with the basket. One cone on the T of the far deuce box as the target. Resting players stand behind the far baseline and rank each serve as slow, medium or fast; a server alone calls the intended speed before the toss and judges honestly.
instructions: Serve three serves at the T: the first at sixty percent pace, the second at eighty, the third at full pace, all with the same swing shape.
The caller ranks the three; score one if they are ranked in the order served, plus one for each serve that lands within a racket length of the cone.
Six sets of three, then rotate.
Second round: the server picks the order and the caller must name the speeds correctly.
Third round: the slow serve must be a heavy slice, the fast one flat.
coaching_points: Change the racket-head speed, not the swing length; the slow serve is a full swing at a slow tempo.
Toss and rhythm identical at every speed; speed is the last thing added.
On the slow serve, hit up more so it still carries to the T.
On the fast serve, keep the toss slightly in front and drive up through the legs.
progressions: Five speeds: fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty and one hundred percent.
The caller must rank the serves before they bounce.
Same drill at the wide target.
regressions: Two speeds: slow and fast.
Serve from a metre inside the baseline.
Score only serves in the box, no ranking.

name: Return Reaction: Serves from the Service Line
summary: Halves the returner's reaction time by having the server serve at full pace from the service line, so the block becomes automatic.
setup: Server stands on the far service line at the centre with the basket, serving at full pace into the near boxes, so the returner has about half the normal time. Returner behind the near baseline. No targets: any return over the net into the singles court counts.
instructions: Server serves at full pace from the service line, alternating boxes.
Returner blocks the ball back into the court, forehand or backhand, with no backswing.
Score one for every return in the court; count out of ten.
Ten serves, then swap roles.
Second round: the returner starts a metre inside the baseline.
coaching_points: Racket in front of the body at chest height before the serve; there is no time to take it back.
Split step as the toss goes up, not on contact; the ball arrives too fast to wait.
Meet the ball in front and let it rebound; a firm wrist and a still head are the whole stroke.
Turn the shoulders, not the arm: a small turn each way is enough.
progressions: Server moves a metre inside the service line.
Returns must land past the far service line.
Server serves to either box without a pattern.
regressions: Server serves from two metres behind the service line.
Server serves at three-quarter pace.
Returner may catch the ball on the strings first, then return the next one.

name: Catch, Then Volley: Hands First at the Net
summary: Introduces the volley as a catch in front of the body, moving from hand catch to racket catch to a blocked volley.
setup: Feeder stands on the far side a metre behind the net at the centre with the basket, tossing underarm. Volleyer stands on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side, racket held out in front at chest height. Extra players queue behind the volleyer, a metre apart.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball gently to the volleyer's forehand side at chest height.
First five: the volleyer catches the ball in the free hand out in front, then drops it.
Next five: the volleyer catches it on the racket strings, holding the racket in front like a plate.
Next five: the volleyer blocks it back over the net to the feeder with no swing.
Rotate, then repeat on the backhand side.
coaching_points: Hands in front: catch the ball where you can see both the ball and your hand.
Step towards the ball with the opposite foot as you catch or block.
No backswing: the racket starts in front and stays in front.
Keep the racket head above the wrist; a dropped head sends the ball into the net.
progressions: Skip the catches and go straight to the block.
Feeder tosses alternately to the forehand and backhand sides.
Feeder tosses from three metres behind the net.
regressions: Feeder tosses from the same side of the net, two metres away.
Use a red ball.
Volleyer catches only, until ten in a row are clean.

name: Volley Punch to the Hoop
summary: Builds a short punching volley by aiming tossed balls cross-court into a hoop on the far side.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, tossing underarm over the net. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. A hoop on the far side in the middle of the service box diagonally across from the volleyer. Extra players queue behind the volleyer.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball to the volleyer's forehand at shoulder height.
Volleyer punches the volley cross-court into the hoop.
Score one for the box, three for the hoop; ten volleys, then rotate.
Second round: backhand volleys, with the hoop moved to the other far box.
Third round: the feeder alternates sides without warning.
coaching_points: Short punch from the shoulder; the racket moves the length of your forearm, no more.
Contact in front of the body with the racket face slightly open.
Step across with the opposite foot as you punch.
Racket head above the wrist, and the wrist firm through contact.
progressions: Move the hoop to the back corner of the far box.
Feeder tosses lower, at waist height.
Feeder hits the feed with a racket from the far baseline.
regressions: Replace the hoop with the whole far box.
Feeder tosses from the same side of the net, three metres away.
Use a red ball.

name: Partner Volley-Volley Count
summary: A cooperative volley rally across the net with no bounce allowed, counted out loud and banked in tens.
setup: Two players facing each other across the net, each two metres from it on the same side of the centre line, rackets up in front. Basket at the net post. No other equipment; the ball may not bounce.
instructions: Player A starts with a gentle self-toss volley to B's forehand.
Volley back and forth without a bounce, counting out loud.
A rally of ten banks a 'ten'; aim for three tens.
Once three tens are banked, play forehand volleys only, then backhand volleys only.
Finish with a round where both players take one step back to three metres.
coaching_points: Rackets up between every volley: the ball is back before you know it.
Block, do not swing; aim for your partner's racket, not past it.
Bend the knees for a low ball instead of dropping the racket head.
Step in with the opposite foot on every volley, then step back to ready.
progressions: Both players step back to the service line.
Alternate forehand and backhand volleys strictly.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Allow one bounce on each side.
Players stand one metre from the net.
Use a red ball.

name: Overhead Catch and Throw
summary: Builds the overhead's turn-and-point preparation by catching lobs above the head and throwing them back with a serving action.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, throwing gentle high lobs underarm over the net. Player on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side, racket in the hitting hand and the free hand ready. Extra players queue behind the player.
instructions: Feeder lobs a ball high to land near the player.
Player turns sideways, points at the ball with the free hand, and catches it above the head in that hand.
Player then throws the ball overarm back over the net to the feeder, as if serving.
Five catch-and-throws, then five where the player lets the racket reach up and touch the ball instead of catching it.
Rotate, then repeat with the feeder lobbing a little deeper each round.
coaching_points: Turn sideways first; a square-on player cannot get under the ball.
Point at the ball with the free hand until the other hand catches it.
Catch and throw above the head, not in front of the face.
Small steps back, never a backward run.
progressions: Catch above the head with the racket hand while the racket is held in the free hand.
Feeder lobs a metre deeper each time.
Replace the throw with an overhead hit into the far box.
regressions: Feeder lobs from the same side of the net, three metres away.
Use a red ball.
Catch in two hands.

name: Overhead off a Gentle Lob into the Big Zone
summary: First overheads off soft hand-fed lobs, with the whole far court past the service line as the target.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, tossing gentle lobs over the net by hand. Player on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. Two cones on the far service line mark the front edge of the big zone: the whole far court past the service line. Extra players queue behind the player.
instructions: Feeder lobs a ball just high enough to clear the player's reach.
Player turns, points, and hits an overhead into the far court past the cones.
Score one for a ball past the service line; ten overheads, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder lobs so the player must take two steps back first.
Third round: the player must hit the overhead cross-court.
coaching_points: Turn sideways and get the racket up behind the head as the lob goes up.
Point at the ball with the free hand and keep it up until the racket comes through.
Hit the ball out in front, slightly to the racket side, at full stretch.
Snap the racket over the top of the ball, finishing across the body.
progressions: Only balls landing past a throwdown line two metres inside the baseline count.
Feeder lobs deeper so the player must retreat with crossover steps.
Feeder hits the lob with a racket from the far baseline.
regressions: Feeder lobs from the same side of the net, three metres in front of the player.
Use an orange ball.
Player catches the lob on the racket first, then throws it down and hits the bounce.

name: Volley Footwork: Step Across on Each Volley
summary: Pairs each volley with a step across onto a throwdown so the feet and the punch learn to happen together.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the centre line, standing behind two throwdowns placed a step forward and a step apart: the left one for the left foot's forehand-volley step, the right one for the right foot's backhand-volley step. Extra players queue behind the volleyer.
instructions: Feeder tosses alternately to the forehand and backhand at chest height.
Volleyer steps across onto the matching throwdown as they volley: left foot for the forehand, right foot for the backhand.
Volley back to the feeder; score one for each volley where the foot lands on the throwdown.
Ten volleys, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder does not alternate; the volleyer must read the side.
coaching_points: Step across, not sideways: the front foot lands in front of the body towards the net.
The step and the punch happen together.
Back to the ready position between volleys, racket up in front.
Weight on the front foot at contact, never rocking back.
progressions: Move the throwdowns a bigger step forward.
Feeder tosses lower so the knees must bend as well.
Feeder hits the feed with a racket from the far baseline.
regressions: Feeder calls the side before each toss.
Feeder tosses from the same side of the net, three metres away.
Use a red ball.

name: Feed, Volley, Point: Mini Game in the Boxes
summary: Starts each point with a volley off a feed, then plays it out inside the service boxes so beginners volley under game pressure.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket; a second player two metres from the near net as the volleyer. Cones on the singles sidelines at both service lines mark the playing area: all four service boxes. With four players, the two others wait behind the far baseline and rotate in after each game.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball to the volleyer; the volleyer volleys it into the far boxes.
The point is then live: the feeder plays the volley back and the point continues inside the boxes.
The volleyer must stay in front of the service line; the feeder may go anywhere in their boxes.
First to five, then rotate roles.
Second game: the feeder may lob once per point.
coaching_points: First volley deep into the far box, then get ready; the point is not over.
Rackets up between shots, feet moving.
Volley to the feeder's feet, not their racket.
Bend the knees for a low ball instead of dropping the racket head.
progressions: Extend the area two metres behind the far service line for the feeder.
The volleyer must win the point with a volley, not off a bounce.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Cooperate for three balls before the point becomes live.
Allow the volleyer one bounce per point.
Use a red ball.

name: Volley Reaction: Two-Ball Toss
summary: Speeds up the reset between volleys by tossing two balls a second apart, forehand then backhand.
setup: Feeder stands on the far side a metre behind the net at the centre, a ball in each hand and the basket at their feet. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the centre line, racket up. Extra players queue behind the volleyer.
instructions: Feeder tosses two balls in quick succession, one to the forehand then one to the backhand, about a second apart.
Volleyer punches both back over the net, forehand then backhand, with no time to reset the racket.
Score one for each ball back over the net; ten pairs, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder chooses the order.
Third round: three balls in a row.
coaching_points: Racket back to the middle immediately after the first volley; the second ball is already in the air.
Small steps between balls; there is no time for a big step.
Contact in front on both; reaching behind means the ball was late.
Breathe out on each punch; holding the breath stiffens the arm.
progressions: Feeder tosses from two metres behind the net.
Reduce the gap between the two balls to half a second.
Add a third ball to the body.
regressions: Two seconds between balls.
Feeder tosses both balls to the forehand.
Use a red ball.

name: Volley-Only Points in the Boxes
summary: Live points inside the service boxes where the ball may never bounce, so every shot is a volley under pressure.
setup: Both players inside their service boxes, starting two metres from the net on the same side of the centre line. Cones on the singles sidelines at both service lines mark the playing area: the four service boxes. Basket at the net post. The ball may not bounce on either side.
instructions: Player A starts with a gentle self-toss volley.
Play the point out with volleys only; a ball that bounces loses the point for the player who let it bounce.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: a volley that lands past the far service line loses the point, so everything stays soft.
Third game: points can be won only with a volley that lands in the far box on the other side of the centre line.
coaching_points: Racket up and in front between every volley; the next ball is a second away.
Volley at your opponent's feet, not their chest; a low ball is the hardest to volley.
Move forward to the ball with small steps; standing still lets it drop.
Firm wrist, short punch; the closer you are, the shorter the swing.
progressions: Extend the area to two metres behind each service line.
Allow a bounce only on your own side, once per point.
Play to fifteen with the loser of each point starting the next volley.
regressions: Allow one bounce per side.
Cooperate for four volleys before the point goes live.
Use an orange ball.

name: Low Volley: Lift It Over from Below the Net
summary: Teaches the low volley by feeding balls that dip below net height, so the player learns to bend and lift with an open face.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting balls that arrive below net height at the volleyer's feet. Volleyer on the near service line at the centre, moving in one step for each ball. A throwdown on the far service line marks the depth target: volleys should land near it, not short. Extra players queue behind the volleyer.
instructions: Feeder sends a ball that dips below net height as it reaches the volleyer.
Volleyer bends, gets the racket head below the ball with the face open, and lifts the volley over the net to land near the far throwdown.
Score one for a volley over the net, two for one that lands within a racket length of the throwdown.
Ten volleys alternating forehand and backhand, then rotate.
Second round: the volleyer starts a metre inside the service line so the ball is even lower.
coaching_points: Bend from the knees, not the waist; get the eyes down to the height of the ball.
Open the racket face and let the ball climb over the net; do not hit down on a low ball.
Firm wrist, soft grip: the lift comes from the legs coming up, not the wrist flicking.
Contact in front of the front knee with the racket head level with the wrist, not below it.
progressions: Feeder hits the feed harder from the far baseline.
Volleys must land past the far service line.
Feeder alternates a low ball with a chest-height ball so the volleyer must adjust height.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm from just behind the net.
Volleyer starts at the net and lets the ball come to waist height.
Use a green ball.

name: Overhead: Turn, Point, Hit
summary: Builds the overhead around three called actions, turn sideways, point at the ball, hit, off racket-fed lobs into the near box.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, lobbing with the racket to land inside the near service box. Player on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. Two cones on the far service line at the singles sidelines mark the target zone: the two far service boxes. Extra players queue behind the player.
instructions: Feeder lobs a ball to land inside the near service box.
Player says 'turn' as they turn sideways, 'point' as the free hand points at the ball, and hits the overhead into the far boxes.
Score one for the far boxes, two for the box diagonally opposite.
Ten overheads, then rotate.
Second round: the player says nothing and the feeder checks that the turn and the point still happen.
coaching_points: Turn sideways as the lob leaves the feeder's racket; the turn comes before the racket goes up.
Point at the ball with the free hand and keep it up until the racket swings.
Reach up: contact at full stretch in front of the head, not behind it.
Hit the ball down into the court with the wrist snapping over the top.
progressions: Feeder lobs deeper so the player must move back two steps before the turn.
Only the diagonal box counts.
Feeder lobs from the far baseline with more height.
regressions: Feeder lobs by hand from the far service line.
Player catches the lob above the head first, then throws it down and hits it after the bounce.
Use an orange ball.

name: Half-Volley Pick-Up on the Way In
summary: Trains the half-volley met at the service line while moving forward, so the approach to the net survives a ball at the feet.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting balls with the racket to land at the volleyer's feet around the near service line. Volleyer starts two metres behind the near service line on the centre line and moves in on every ball. A cone on the near service line marks where the ball should be met. Extra players queue behind the volleyer.
instructions: Feeder hits a ball to land just in front of the cone, at the volleyer's feet as they move in.
Volleyer takes the ball on the half-volley, just after the bounce, and sends it back over the net into the far boxes.
After each ball, the volleyer continues to the net, touches it with the racket, and jogs back to the start.
Ten balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates a half-volley ball with a chest-height volley.
coaching_points: Keep moving through the ball; stopping to play the half-volley is what makes it pop up.
Racket face slightly closed and low, knees bent, contact just after the bounce in front of the front foot.
Block it, do not swing; the bounce gives the ball all the pace it needs.
Head still and low through contact; look at the bounce, not the far court.
progressions: Feeder hits harder from the far baseline.
Half-volleys must land past the far service line.
Volleyer plays the half-volley and then a real volley off a second feed.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm from just over the net.
Volleyer starts on the service line and does not move in.
Use a green ball.

name: Net vs Baseline: Cooperative Rally Count
summary: A cooperative rally between a net player and a baseliner down one half of the court, counting volleys and banking tens.
setup: One player at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side; the other on the far baseline on the same side of the court. Basket at the net post. The rally goes volley, groundstroke, volley, groundstroke, cooperatively, down one half of the court.
instructions: Baseline player starts with a self-drop groundstroke to the net player.
Net player volleys back deep to the baseline player; count each volley out loud.
Rally to an error; a rally of ten volleys banks a point.
Swap roles every three minutes.
Second round: the net player alternates forehand and backhand volleys by aiming to either side of the baseliner.
coaching_points: Net player: volley deep and high enough to reach the baseline; a short volley ends the cooperation.
Baseline player: hit to the net player's hip, not past them.
Net player: split step as the baseliner makes contact, every time.
Both: aim for rhythm, not pace; the count is the score.
progressions: Net player must volley past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
Baseline player mixes in a lob every fifth ball.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Baseline player stands on the service line.
Allow the net player one bounce per rally.
Use an orange ball.

name: Approach and Two Volleys
summary: A three-ball sequence, approach shot, deep first volley and finishing volley, so the whole trip to the net is trained in one go.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Player on the near baseline on the deuce side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline marks the target for the approach and the first volley. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder hits a short ball inside the near service line; the player moves in and hits an approach shot down the line, deep past the throwdown line.
Feeder immediately feeds a second ball; the player volleys it deep.
Feeder feeds a third ball; the player finishes with a volley into the open court.
Score one for each of the three balls in its target; three balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder chooses which side the volleys go to without warning.
coaching_points: Approach down the line and follow it in on the same side; the volley position is a step to that side of the centre.
Split step at the service line as the feeder makes contact with the second ball.
First volley deep, second volley to the open court: depth before angle.
Keep moving forward through the sequence; the third ball is met a metre from the net.
progressions: Feeder hits the second and third balls harder.
Add a fourth ball: a lob that must be dealt with.
Feeder mixes the short ball to either side so the approach may be a backhand.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm instead of hitting with the racket.
Two balls only: approach and one volley.
Widen the target to anywhere in the far court.

name: Overhead Retreat: Cross Over, Back and Hit
summary: Trains the footwork for a lob over the head: turn, crossover steps back behind the ball, hit, and close in again.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, lobbing with the racket over the player's head. Player starts at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side. A cone on the near service line marks how far back the lobs should push the player. Extra players queue beside the player, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder lobs over the player's head to land around the near service line.
Player turns sideways, retreats with crossover steps behind the ball, and hits the overhead into the far court.
After the overhead, the player closes back to the net position before the next lob.
Eight overheads, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates a deep lob with a short lob that can be hit without retreating.
coaching_points: Turn and cross over immediately; backpedalling facing the net is slow and unbalanced.
Get behind the ball so the contact is in front of the head, not above or behind it.
Point with the free hand while retreating; it keeps the shoulders turned.
Push off the back foot into the overhead, then close to the net again.
progressions: Feeder lobs deeper, to the baseline.
Overheads must land past the far service line.
Feeder follows the lob with a passing shot that must be volleyed after closing.
regressions: Feeder lobs shorter, inside the near service box.
Player may let the lob bounce and hit it after the bounce.
Feeder lobs by hand.

name: Drop Volley: Touch into the Hoop
summary: Develops soft hands at the net by turning firm feeds into drop volleys that die in a hoop just over the net.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting firm balls at the volleyer with the racket. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. A hoop on the far side a metre behind the net, straight in front of the volleyer. Extra players queue behind the volleyer.
instructions: Feeder hits a firm ball at chest height to the volleyer.
Volleyer softens the hands and drops the volley into the hoop just over the net.
Score two for the hoop, one for a ball that bounces twice inside the far service box.
Ten drop volleys alternating forehand and backhand, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates a firm ball, which must be dropped, with a slow ball, which must be punched deep.
coaching_points: Loosen the grip at contact; the racket gives with the ball like catching an egg.
Open the face slightly and cut under the ball so it checks.
Keep the racket in front and the swing tiny; the ball's pace is absorbed, not added to.
Contact out in front where the hands can be soft; a late ball cannot be dropped.
progressions: Move the hoop half a metre towards the sideline for an angled drop.
Feeder hits harder from the far baseline.
Feeder follows the drop volley in and plays the point out.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm instead of hitting with the racket.
Replace the hoop with the whole far service box.
Use a green ball.

name: Reflex Volleys: One Attacks, One Blocks
summary: Close-range volley exchanges with fixed roles, one player punching hard and the other absorbing, to build reflexes and soft hands together.
setup: Two players across the net from each other, each two metres from it on the same side of the centre line. One is the attacker, the other the blocker. Basket at the net post. No bounces allowed.
instructions: Attacker starts with a firm volley at the blocker's body.
Blocker absorbs it and volleys back softly to the attacker's racket; the attacker volleys hard again, and so on.
Count the exchanges; a rally of eight banks a point for the pair.
Swap roles every two minutes.
Second round: the attacker may volley to either side of the blocker, not only the body.
coaching_points: Blocker: racket in front at chest height, elbows bent, and let the ball hit the strings; no swing at all.
Attacker: punch through the ball with the wrist firm; aim at the blocker's hip.
Both: eyes on the ball to the strings; at this range you cannot track the opponent.
Both: small split as the other player makes contact; the feet stay light.
progressions: Players move to one metre from the net.
Attacker volleys to the sides so the blocker must move.
No roles: both attack.
regressions: Attacker volleys at three-quarter pace.
Players stand at the service line.
Allow one bounce per rally.

name: Volley Direction: Cross or Line on the Call
summary: Trains volley placement off driven balls, directing each volley into a cross-court or down-the-line corner box on the feeder's call.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, driving balls with the racket. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. Two cone targets on the far side: a two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner and a two-metre cone box in the far down-the-line corner, both against the baseline. Extra players queue beside the volleyer, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder calls 'cross' or 'line' as the ball is struck, then drives it at the volleyer.
Volleyer directs the volley into the called box.
Score two for the box, one for the correct half, zero for the wrong direction.
Ten volleys, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder calls only as the ball crosses the net.
coaching_points: Cross-court: contact further in front with the face angled; down the line: contact later with the face square.
Keep the punch short for both; direction comes from the face and the contact point, not the swing.
Step across towards the target with the opposite foot.
Racket head above the wrist for both, even on the low ball.
progressions: Shrink the boxes to one metre.
Feeder drives the ball harder from the baseline.
Feeder calls after the ball crosses the net.
regressions: Widen the targets to the whole far halves.
Feeder tosses underarm from the far service line.
Feeder calls before striking the ball.

name: Overhead Scissor Kick off the Deep Lob
summary: Adds the scissor-kick jump to the overhead so deep lobs can still be hit down instead of let bounce.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, lobbing with the racket over the player's head towards the near service line. Player starts at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target. Extra players queue beside the player, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder lobs deep over the player's head.
Player turns, retreats with crossover steps, and hits the overhead with a scissor kick, jumping off the back foot and landing on the front foot.
Aim past the far throwdown line; score one for the far court, two for past the line.
Eight overheads, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder mixes deep lobs with short lobs; the short ones are hit without jumping.
coaching_points: Get behind the ball first; the jump is for reach, not for chasing.
Jump off the back foot, hit at the top, land on the front foot with the back leg kicking forward.
Free hand points at the ball until the racket comes through.
Hit down and through the ball with a full snap; a scissor-kick overhead pushed safe lands short.
progressions: Feeder lobs to the baseline.
Overheads must land in the far corner boxes.
Feeder follows the overhead with a passing shot to be volleyed.
regressions: Feeder lobs shorter so no jump is needed.
Player lets the deep lob bounce and hits it after the bounce.
Feeder lobs by hand from the far service line.

name: Poach Volley: Cross the Middle on the Feed
summary: Teaches the doubles poach, timing the move across the middle to the feeder's contact and finishing the volley at a target.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline on the deuce side with the basket, hitting cross-court drives as if returning serve in doubles. Net player on the near side two metres from the net on the ad side, in the doubles net position. A cone on the near centre line marks where the poach should be made; a second cone in the middle of the far ad service box marks the poach target. Extra players queue beside the net player, outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a cross-court return towards the near deuce side.
Net player moves across the middle as the feeder makes contact, intercepts the ball at the cone, and volleys it at the far target.
Score one for a volley in the far court, two for the target.
Eight poaches, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder sometimes hits down the line instead; a net player who has already left the line loses a point.
coaching_points: Move as the feeder's racket meets the ball, not before; an early move gives it away.
Cross diagonally forward towards the net, not sideways along it.
Volley at a sharp angle or at the target's feet; the poach ends the point, it does not restart it.
After the poach, carry on through: land beyond the centre and hold the new side.
progressions: Feeder drives harder and lower.
Add a signal: the net player poaches only when a partner behind them calls 'go'.
Play the point out after the poach with the feeder alone.
regressions: Feeder tosses the return underarm from the far service line.
Net player starts on the centre line so the move is shorter.
Widen the target to the whole far court.

name: Volley-Overhead Combination: Two-Ball Feed
summary: Pairs a deep volley with an immediate lob to hit, so the net player learns to reset after the volley instead of admiring it.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Player at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target for both shots. Extra players queue beside the player, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a ball at the player, who volleys it deep past the throwdown line.
Feeder immediately lobs; the player retreats and hits the overhead deep.
Score one per ball past the line; two balls, then the next player steps in.
Ten pairs each round.
Second round: the feeder reverses the order, lob first, then a drive at the player who has closed back in.
coaching_points: After the volley, expect the lob: keep the feet moving and the racket up.
Turn sideways on the lob immediately; the volley finish must not leave you square.
Volley deep, not hard; the overhead is where the point is won.
Close back to the net after the overhead as if a third ball were coming.
progressions: Add a third ball: a passing shot after the overhead.
Feeder lobs deeper so a scissor kick is needed.
Both balls must land in the far corner boxes.
regressions: Feeder waits until the player has recovered before the lob.
Feeder lobs shorter so no retreat is needed.
Feeder tosses the first ball underarm.

name: Swinging Volley off the Floating Ball
summary: Teaches players to take a slow floating ball out of the air with a full topspin swing instead of waiting for the bounce.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, hitting slow, high, floating balls with the racket to land around the near service line. Player on the near baseline on the deuce side. A two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner is the target. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder floats a slow ball that would land near the near service line.
Player moves in and takes the ball out of the air with a full topspin swing, a swinging volley, into the cone box.
Score two for the box, one for the far court.
Ten swinging volleys, then rotate.
Second round: the player follows the swinging volley to the net and plays a second ball fed as a volley.
coaching_points: Move through the ball: the contact is made while stepping forward, not from a stop.
Same swing as a topspin groundstroke, with the contact at shoulder height and out in front.
Brush up and over the ball; a flat swinging volley flies long.
Decide early: as soon as the ball floats, commit to taking it in the air.
progressions: Shrink the box to one metre.
Feeder floats the ball lower so the decision is harder.
Feeder follows with a passing shot after the swinging volley.
regressions: Feeder tosses the floating ball by hand from the far service line.
Widen the target to the whole far half.
Player may let the ball bounce and hit it on the rise instead.

name: Net vs Baseline Points: Win It in Three
summary: Live points between a net player and a baseliner where the net player must finish within three shots or lose the point.
setup: One player at the near net, two metres from it on the centre line; the other on the far baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. The baseline player starts each point with a self-drop drive; the singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Baseline player starts the point with a drive at the net player.
Net player must win the point within three volleys or overheads; if the rally goes past three, the baseline player wins the point.
The baseline player may lob, pass or drive; the net player may not let the ball bounce.
First to eleven, then swap roles.
Second game: the net player must win within two shots.
coaching_points: First volley deep to the baseliner's backhand, second volley to the open court: that is the three-shot plan.
Split step on every contact by the baseliner, especially when you think the point is won.
On the lob, turn and hit the overhead; do not let it bounce even when tempted.
Baseliner: the low dipping ball at the net player's feet is worth more than a pass.
progressions: Net player must win within two shots.
Baseliner gets one free lob per point that the net player must let bounce.
Play games to fifteen with the net player starting from the service line.
regressions: Net player may win within five shots.
Baseliner may not lob.
Cooperate for two balls before the point goes live.

name: Volley Touch Ladder: Drop, Angle, Deep
summary: Three volleys in a row to three different targets, a drop, an angle and a deep ball, so touch and direction are trained from one ready position.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting medium-pace balls with the racket. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. Three targets on the far side: a hoop a metre behind the net straight ahead for the drop, a cone in the far alley level with the service line for the angle, and a two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner for the deep volley. Extra players queue beside the volleyer, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds three balls in a row; the volleyer plays a drop volley into the hoop, an angled volley past the alley cone, and a deep volley into the corner box, in that order.
Score one per target hit; three balls, then rotate.
After everyone has had three rounds, the feeder calls the order at random.
Fourth round: the volleyer calls their own shot before each feed.
Finish with three balls where all three must be hit from the backhand side.
coaching_points: Drop: soft hands and an open face, the racket gives on contact.
Angle: contact well in front with the face turned early; the ball crosses the net low and wide.
Deep: firm wrist, short punch through the ball, finish pointing at the box.
Same ready position for all three; the difference is decided in the last half metre.
progressions: Shrink the deep box to one metre and move the angle cone further back.
Feeder drives harder from the far baseline.
Feeder calls the shot after the ball crosses the net.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm instead of hitting with the racket.
Two targets only: drop and deep.
Widen all targets: the far service box for the drop, the alley for the angle, the far half for the deep volley.

name: Ready Position and Split Step on the Toss
summary: Teaches beginners to split step as the feeder's hand releases the ball, judged and scored on timing.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket, facing the hitter. Hitter on the near service line at the centre, standing on a throwdown in the ready position. Extra players queue behind the hitter.
instructions: Feeder holds the ball up, then tosses underarm to either side, a metre from the hitter.
Hitter split-steps as the ball leaves the feeder's hand, moves to the ball, and hits it gently back to the feeder.
Feeder calls 'early' or 'late' for each split; score one for a split that lands as the ball leaves the hand.
Ten balls, then swap the hitter.
Second round: the feeder sometimes fakes the toss and keeps the ball; a hitter who moves anyway loses a point.
coaching_points: Feet shoulder-width, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet before every ball.
Hop as the feeder's hand starts to move; land as the ball leaves it.
Land with the feet apart, then push off towards the ball with the outside foot.
Racket in front with both hands at waist height until you know the side.
progressions: Feeder tosses from the far service line, over the net.
Feeder tosses further from the hitter, two metres to either side.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Feeder calls the side before tossing.
Hitter catches the ball instead of hitting it.
Use a red ball.

name: Forward and Back: Short Ball, Deep Ball
summary: Alternates a short and a deep toss so beginners learn to run forward through a ball and turn to get behind a deep one.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket. Hitter starts on the near baseline at the centre mark. Two cones on the centre line: one a metre inside the service line for the short ball, one a metre inside the baseline for the deep ball. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder alternates a short toss to the front cone and a deep toss to the back cone.
Hitter runs forward to hit the short ball, then turns and gets back behind the deep ball, hits it, and so on.
Every ball is hit over the net into the far court.
Eight balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder chooses the order without warning.
coaching_points: Forward: run with the racket already back and hit while the feet are still moving.
Back: turn sideways and take crossover steps, do not backpedal facing the net.
Get behind the deep ball before it bounces, then step forward into it.
After the short ball, stop with a split step before turning to run back.
progressions: Move the deep cone a metre behind the baseline.
Feeder tosses the next ball as soon as the last one is hit.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Move the cones a metre closer together.
Feeder waits until the hitter is set before tossing.
Use a red ball.

name: Agility Ladder, Then Hit
summary: Runs a ladder pattern straight into a fed ball so quick feet finish with a balanced hit, in a fast-moving queue.
setup: Agility ladder laid along the near baseline from the singles sideline towards the centre mark. Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket. Players queue at the sideline end of the ladder, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: First player runs the ladder with two feet in every box.
As they step off the last box, the feeder tosses a ball to the forehand; the player hits it over the net and jogs to the back of the queue.
Next player goes as soon as the ball is hit.
Three runs each with two feet in, then three runs with an in-in-out-out sideways pattern.
Last round: the feeder tosses to the backhand.
coaching_points: Quick feet, small steps: the ladder is about rhythm, not speed over the ground.
Eyes up on the feeder for the last two boxes, not on your feet.
Step off the ladder into a split step before moving to the ball.
Hit the ball from a balanced stance; the run is over once the ball is in the air.
progressions: Add a second pattern: lateral shuffles through the ladder.
Feeder tosses the ball before the player reaches the last box.
Two balls after the ladder: forehand then backhand.
regressions: Walk the ladder before running it.
Feeder waits until the player is set before tossing.
Use a red ball.

name: Two-Ball Left-Right Recovery
summary: A forehand-side ball then a backhand-side ball, with a side-step recovery to a throwdown between them, timed by the feeder.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket. Hitter starts on a throwdown on the near baseline at the centre mark. A cone two metres either side of the throwdown marks where the two feeds bounce. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball to the forehand cone; the hitter moves, hits it over the net, and shuffles back to the throwdown.
As the hitter touches the throwdown, the feeder tosses the second ball to the backhand cone.
Two balls, then the hitter jogs to the queue and the next player steps on.
Four rounds each; score one for every ball over the net and one for every recovery that reaches the throwdown before the next toss.
Last round: three balls, forehand, backhand, forehand.
coaching_points: Side steps back to the throwdown, facing the net; do not turn and run.
Split step on the throwdown as the feeder tosses.
First step to the ball is a big one, the last step is small so you are balanced when you hit.
Recover as soon as the ball leaves the strings; do not stand and admire it.
progressions: Move the cones a metre wider.
Feeder tosses the second ball before the hitter reaches the throwdown.
Switch from an orange ball to a green ball.
regressions: Move the cones a metre closer.
Feeder waits until the hitter is still on the throwdown before tossing.
Use a red ball.

name: Rolled Ball: First-Step Reaction
summary: A partner rolls balls to either side and the mover must push off and stop them with the racket before they pass a cone line.
setup: Two players on the near side of the court. The roller kneels on the near service line at the centre with the basket; the mover stands on the near baseline at the centre mark, racket in hand, facing the roller. A cone two metres either side of the mover marks the limit of the rolls.
instructions: Roller rolls a ball along the ground towards either cone.
Mover pushes off with the first step, gets to the ball before it passes the cone line, and stops it with the racket face on the ground.
Roll the ball back to the roller and recover to the centre mark.
Ten rolls, then swap roles.
Second round: the roller fakes one direction and rolls the other.
coaching_points: Push off the outside foot; the first step goes towards the ball, not upwards.
Stay low as you move; the ball is on the ground and so is your racket.
Recover with side steps facing the roller so the next roll is not a surprise.
Small split as the roller's hand moves, then go.
progressions: Roller rolls the ball faster along the ground.
Move the cones a metre wider.
Mover must stop the ball and hit it back along the ground in one motion.
regressions: Roller calls the side before rolling.
Move the cones a metre closer.
Mover stops the ball with the foot instead of the racket.

name: Run, Hit, Run: Team Relay
summary: A team relay where each runner sprints to a cone, hits a fed ball over the net, and sprints back to tag the next runner.
setup: Two teams lined up behind the near baseline, one at each singles sideline. Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket. A cone on the near service line in front of each team marks where the runner stops to hit.
instructions: On 'go', the first runner from each team sprints to their cone.
Feeder tosses a ball to the runner at the cone; the runner hits it over the net into the far court.
Runner sprints back and tags the next teammate, who goes immediately.
First team through everyone twice wins; a ball that misses the far court costs that runner an extra run.
Second race: runners must hit a backhand.
coaching_points: Split step at the cone before the toss; a running swing goes anywhere.
Racket back while running the last three steps to the cone.
Hit up and over: the far court is big, the net is the only obstacle.
Sprint back on the outside so the next runner has a clear lane.
progressions: Move the cones to the near baseline so the run is longer.
The ball must land past the far service line.
Runners hit two balls, forehand then backhand, before running back.
regressions: Move the cones to the net so the run is short.
Feeder tosses only after the runner is still.
Use a red ball.

name: Deep Ball Retreat: Back Behind the Baseline
summary: Trains the turn-and-retreat footwork for a deep, high ball so it is played at hip height from behind the baseline, then recovered from.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting deep, high balls with the racket to land within a metre of the near baseline. Hitter starts on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown two metres behind the baseline marks how far the retreat should go. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder hits a deep, high ball.
Hitter turns sideways, retreats with crossover steps to behind the throwdown, lets the ball drop to hip height, and hits it back deep over the net.
After the shot, the hitter moves back up to the baseline with side steps.
Eight balls alternating forehand and backhand, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates a deep ball with a medium-length ball that must be hit from the baseline without retreating.
coaching_points: Turn first, then run; retreating square-on to the net is slow.
Get behind the bounce so the ball comes down to you, not up at you.
Step forward into the shot from the retreat position; the momentum goes back towards the net.
Recover up to the baseline straight away; do not stay behind the throwdown.
progressions: Feeder hits deeper and higher.
Shots must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
Feeder feeds the next ball as the hitter reaches the baseline.
regressions: Feeder hits shorter so the retreat is one step.
Feeder tosses the deep ball by hand from the far baseline.
Hitter may let the ball bounce twice.

name: Shuffle Rally: Side Steps Only
summary: A cooperative rally inside a narrow lane where only side steps are allowed, so recovery footwork becomes a habit.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Two cones on each baseline, two metres either side of the centre mark, mark the lane each player must stay inside. Basket at the net post. The rally is cooperative and down the middle.
instructions: Rally cooperatively down the middle; every ball is aimed between the partner's cones.
Both players may move only with side steps: no crossover steps, no running.
A crossover step, or a ball outside the cones, ends the rally.
Count the rally; a rally of fifteen banks a point, first to three.
Second round: cones moved a metre wider so the balls can go a little further from the middle.
coaching_points: Wide base, knees bent, and push off the outside foot for every side step.
Recover to the centre mark after every ball even when the next one is coming down the middle.
Small adjustment steps before the swing; big steps are for running, which is banned here.
Split step as the partner makes contact.
progressions: Move the cones a metre wider.
Each player must alternate forehand and backhand.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Move the cones a metre closer.
Play from the service lines instead of the baselines.
Use an orange ball.

name: Cone Touch Before the Feed
summary: Forces forward momentum into every shot by starting each ball from a cone touch behind the baseline and hitting on the way in.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter starts on the near baseline at the centre mark. A cone a metre behind the baseline directly behind the hitter; a second cone a metre inside the baseline in front of them. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Hitter touches the back cone with the racket, then moves forward as the feeder feeds.
Hitter hits the ball from around the front cone, moving forward through it, and sends it deep over the net.
Recover to the centre mark, touch the back cone, and go again.
Eight balls alternating forehand and backhand, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder feeds before the hitter has touched the back cone, so the timing is tighter.
coaching_points: Move forward through the ball; the shot is hit while the weight is going towards the net.
Racket back during the forward run, not after you arrive.
Take the ball early, at the top of the bounce or on the rise, since you are moving in.
Recover backwards with side steps facing the net; turn only to touch the cone.
progressions: Move the back cone two metres behind the baseline.
Feeder feeds shorter so the forward run is longer.
Shots must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
regressions: Move the back cone onto the baseline.
Feeder tosses underarm and waits for the cone touch.
Use an orange ball.

name: Figure of Eight Around Two Cones, Then Hit
summary: A figure-of-eight footwork loop around two cones that ends with a live fed ball, so the hit is made with tired, organised feet.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket. Two cones on the near baseline, two metres either side of the centre mark. Hitter starts on the centre mark between them. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Hitter runs a figure of eight around the two cones, side-stepping the straight sections and turning tightly at each cone.
As the hitter passes the centre mark on the second loop, the feeder feeds a ball to either side.
Hitter hits it deep over the net and recovers to the centre mark.
Six repetitions, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder feeds two balls after the figure of eight, one to each side.
coaching_points: Stay low through the turns; standing up at the cone loses the next step.
Side steps on the straights, crossover only at the turns.
Split step as the feeder makes contact, even mid-run.
Balanced stance at contact: if you are still moving sideways when you hit, slow the run down.
progressions: Move the cones a metre wider.
Feeder feeds during the first loop, not the second.
Shots must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
regressions: One loop instead of two.
Feeder waits until the hitter is still at the centre mark.
Use an orange ball.

name: Balance Hold After Contact
summary: Scores the finish of every shot on balance: hold the follow-through on the front foot for two seconds with no extra step.
