setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket, tossing underarm. Hitter on the near service line on the deuce side, on a throwdown. Extra players queue behind the hitter and act as the judge.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball a metre to the hitter's forehand side.
Hitter steps to the ball, hits it over the net, and holds the finish position, balanced on the front foot, for a count of two.
The judge scores one for a clean hold with no extra step, zero for a stumble or a second step.
Ten balls, then rotate.
Second round: alternate forehand and backhand.
coaching_points: Finish with the weight on the front foot and the back foot light; the hips have turned to face the net.
Head still and level through contact; a moving head is what unbalances the finish.
Hitting arm finishes over the shoulder and the free arm across the body to balance it.
If you cannot hold the finish, the last step to the ball was too big.
progressions: Feeder tosses two metres to the side so the hitter must move further.
Hold the finish for a count of three.
Feeder tosses a low ball so the knees must bend as well.
regressions: Feeder tosses straight to the hitter with no movement.
Hold the finish for a count of one.
Hitter catches the ball on the strings and holds that position first.

name: Hit and Sprint to the Net Cone
summary: Every groundstroke is followed by a sprint to the net and a recovery to the baseline, so the next ball is met tired but on time.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline on the deuce side. A cone on the near service line in front of the hitter and a second cone a metre from the net on the same line. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds a ball to the hitter's forehand.
Hitter hits it deep over the net, then sprints to touch the net cone and backpedals to the baseline.
As the hitter reaches the baseline, the feeder feeds the next ball.
Six balls, then rotate.
Second round: the hitter touches only the service-line cone and the feeder feeds sooner.
coaching_points: Sprint as soon as the ball leaves the strings; the shot is finished.
Touch the cone low with the racket, not the hand, so you stay in a tennis posture.
Backpedal only for the first three steps, then turn and side-step the rest.
Split step on the baseline as the feeder makes contact.
progressions: Feeder feeds before the hitter reaches the baseline.
Hitter volleys a second ball at the net cone before backpedalling.
Shots must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
regressions: Touch only the service-line cone.
Feeder waits until the hitter is set on the baseline.
Use an orange ball.

name: Random Feed: Full-Court Coverage, Everything Cross-Court
summary: Feeds anywhere in the court with no pattern so the hitter must read, split, reach and recover on every ball.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket anywhere in the near singles court: short, deep, wide, middle, in no pattern. Hitter starts on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds eight balls anywhere in the court, one every four seconds.
Hitter reaches every ball and hits it cross-court from wherever it is: deep past the throwdown line from the baseline, over the net and in from anywhere short.
Recover towards the centre of the court after every ball; the next feed comes regardless.
Eight balls, then rotate; score one per ball in, two for a deep ball from the baseline.
Second round: everything down the line instead.
coaching_points: Split step on every feed; with no pattern, the split is the only warning you get.
Recover to the middle of the angle the feeder has, not always to the centre mark.
Short ball: move through it and keep moving; deep ball: get behind it and hold the baseline.
Hit high and heavy when late, flat only when early and balanced.
progressions: Feed every three seconds.
Feeder mixes in lobs that must be dealt with in the air.
Balls must land in the far cross-court corner box.
regressions: Feed every six seconds.
Feeder feeds only deep balls, anywhere along the baseline.
Widen the target to anywhere in the far court.

name: Recover to the Right Cone
summary: Teaches recovery position as a decision: after every shot, recover to the cone that bisects the opponent's possible angles.
setup: One player on each baseline. On each baseline, three cones: one on the centre mark and one a metre either side of it. Basket at the net post. Rally cooperatively at rally pace across the whole singles court.
instructions: Rally cooperatively, hitting to all parts of the court.

After each shot, recover to the cone that covers the angle you have just given: cross-court, recover to the cone on the side you hit from; down the line, recover to the cone on the opposite side; down the middle, recover to the centre cone.
Partner calls 'wrong cone' when the recovery misses; a wrong cone ends the rally.
Count rallies; a rally of twelve banks a point, first to three.
Second round: the partner may hit any ball at pace, and the recovery must still be to the right cone.
coaching_points: The recovery spot is the middle of your opponent's angles, not the middle of the court.
Recover with side steps and split as they make contact, on the cone, not on the way to it.
Decide the recovery cone as the ball leaves your strings; you already know where you hit it.
When you are late to the cone, stop and split anyway; a split from the wrong spot beats no split.
progressions: Move the outer cones two metres from the centre mark.
Play the points out after four cooperative balls.
A 'wrong cone' call wins the point for the caller.
regressions: Rally cross-court only, recovering to the one cone on that side.
Move the outer cones half a metre from the centre mark.
Play from the service lines.

name: Split Step Call on the Partner's Contact
summary: A cooperative rally where each player says 'split' as they land, so the timing of the split step is heard and corrected by the partner.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. Cooperative rally across the whole singles court; no other equipment.
instructions: Rally cooperatively at rally pace.
Each player says 'split' out loud at the moment they land their split step, which should be as the partner's racket meets the ball.
The partner listens: a 'split' called after the ball has crossed the net is late and ends the rally.
Count rallies; a rally of twenty banks a point, first to three.
Second round: no calling out loud; the partner calls 'late' when they see a late split.
coaching_points: Leave the ground as the partner's racket starts forward, land as the ball is struck.
Land on the balls of the feet with the feet wider than the shoulders.
The split is small: a few centimetres off the ground is enough.
Push off the outside foot from the split; the first step follows the landing, it does not wait.
progressions: Partner mixes in short balls and lobs; the split must still be on contact.
Play the points out after six cooperative balls.
Rally at match pace.
regressions: Rally from the service lines.
Partner says 'hit' at contact so the split has a sound to match.
Split on the bounce instead of the contact for the first round.

name: Approach Transition: Three Steps, Then Split
summary: Times the transition to the net: approach on the move, three quick steps, a split on the service line as the passing shot is struck, then the volley.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Player on the near baseline on the deuce side. A cone a metre inside the near service line marks where the short feed lands; a throwdown on the near service line, a step towards the centre, marks where the split step should land after the approach. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds a short ball to the cone.
Player moves in, hits the approach shot down the line, takes three quick steps forward and split-steps on the throwdown as the feeder makes contact with the next ball.
Feeder feeds a passing shot; the player volleys it into the far court.
Score one for the approach in, one for a split on the throwdown in time, one for the volley in.
Six sequences, then rotate.
coaching_points: Hit the approach while moving forward; do not stop to hit it.
Three steps, then split: the split must land as the feeder's racket meets the ball, wherever you are.
Split with the feet wide and the racket up in front; the volley comes fast.
Close the net after the volley; the split at the service line is not the finish line.
progressions: Feeder feeds the passing shot sooner.
The approach must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
Feeder mixes a lob with the passing shot.
regressions: Feeder waits until the player has split before feeding the passing shot.
Feeder tosses the passing shot underarm from the far service line.
Remove the volley: approach, three steps, split, then stop.

name: Lateral Defence: Stretch Wide and Recover
summary: Drives balls beyond the sideline so the hitter learns the wide-stance stretch, the high defensive reply and the crossover recovery.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, driving balls wide beyond the near singles sideline on the forehand side. Hitter starts on the near baseline at the centre mark. A cone a metre outside the singles sideline, level with the baseline, marks where the wide ball is met; a throwdown on the centre mark is the recovery point. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline on the backhand side.
instructions: Feeder drives a ball wide to the cone.
Hitter runs, stretches into the ball with a wide stance, hits it back deep cross-court or as a high defensive ball, and recovers to the throwdown with crossover steps then side steps.
Feeder feeds the next ball as the hitter touches the throwdown.
Six balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates wide forehand and wide backhand.
coaching_points: Last step to the wide ball is a big one with the outside foot, knee bent, hip low.
From the stretch, hit up and high: a defensive ball buys time to recover.
Push off the outside foot to start the recovery; the first two steps are crossovers.
Split as the feeder makes contact even if you have not reached the throwdown.
progressions: Move the cone another metre wider.
Feeder feeds the next ball before the hitter reaches the throwdown.
The defensive ball must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
regressions: Move the cone onto the singles sideline.
Feeder waits until the hitter is still on the throwdown.
Feeder tosses the wide ball underarm from the far service line.

name: Low Ball Lunge Pick-Up
summary: Low skidding feeds short and wide teach the long last step, the low hip and the lift needed to get a low ball back over the net.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting low skidding slices with the racket that land short and wide on the near side. Hitter starts on the near service line at the centre. A throwdown a metre inside the near singles sideline on each side marks where the low balls land. Extra players queue behind the hitter.
instructions: Feeder slices a low ball to one of the throwdowns.
Hitter lunges to it with a long last step, gets the racket under the ball, and lifts it back over the net deep.
Recover to the centre with a push off the lunging leg.
Eight balls alternating sides, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder hits the low ball faster so the lunge must be earlier.
coaching_points: Long last step, front knee over the toes, back leg straight; the hip drops, the back does not bend.
Racket head below the ball and the face open before the lunge finishes.
Lift with the legs coming up, not the wrist; the ball must clear the net with margin.
Push back off the front foot to recover; do not stand up first.
progressions: Move the throwdowns onto the singles sideline.
Feeder feeds the next ball as the hitter recovers.
Returns must land past the far service line.
regressions: Move the throwdowns half a metre closer to the centre.
Feeder tosses the low ball underarm instead of slicing it.
Hitter starts a metre closer to the throwdowns.

name: Defence to Offence: Reset, Then Attack
summary: A wide deep ball that must be reset high and deep, followed by a short ball that must be attacked, so the switch from defending to attacking is trained as one movement.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline marks the deep target for the reset ball; a two-metre cone box in each far corner marks the attack targets. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a wide, deep ball; the hitter defends with a high, deep reset past the throwdown line.
Feeder immediately feeds a short ball; the hitter moves in and attacks it into a corner box.
Score one for the reset deep, two for the attack in a box.
Six pairs, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder decides whether the second ball is short or deep again; the hitter must read it and reset again if it is deep.
coaching_points: Under pressure, hit up and high; the reset is measured in seconds bought, not pace.
Recover through the middle immediately; the short ball is coming while you are still moving.
Read the short ball early and move in with the racket already back.
Attack with margin: a deep corner, not the line.
progressions: Feeder feeds the short ball before the reset has landed.
Shrink the corner boxes to one metre.
Add a third ball: a passing shot after the attack that must be volleyed.
regressions: Feeder waits for the hitter to recover before the short ball.
Widen the attack target to the whole far court.
Feeder tosses the wide ball underarm from the far service line.

name: Drop Shot Chase in a Live Rally
summary: A cooperative rally in which either player may drop-shot at any moment, rewarding the chaser who reads it early and sprints.
setup: One player on each baseline. Basket at the net post. A cooperative baseline rally in which either player may drop-shot at any moment; the point is live from the drop shot onwards. Singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Rally cooperatively from the baseline at rally pace.
At any moment either player may play a drop shot; the other must sprint to it and the point is live.
The chaser scores two for winning the point after reaching the drop shot; the dropper scores one for winning it.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: the chaser may reply only with a drop shot of their own or a lob.
coaching_points: Read the drop early: the racket face opens and the swing slows; go on that, not on the bounce.
First three steps are a sprint, the last one is a long low step so the racket gets under the ball.
Play the reply up the line with an open face, or a lob; a cross-court reply opens the court against you.
After the reply, keep moving forward; the next ball will be a pass or a lob, not a rally ball.
progressions: The dropper may follow the drop shot to the net.
The chaser must win the point in two shots or fewer.
Drop shots must be played from behind the baseline.
regressions: Only one player may drop-shot per game.
The dropper announces 'drop' as they hit it.
The chaser may let the drop shot bounce twice in the first game.

name: Defensive Lob from Behind the Baseline, Then Recover
summary: Heavy deep feeds push the hitter back, who must lob deep and use the lob's flight time to recover into the court.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, driving heavy deep balls with the racket. Hitter starts on the near baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target for the lob. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a heavy ball that pushes the hitter well behind the baseline.
Hitter retreats, plays a high defensive lob to land past the far throwdown line, and recovers into the court to the baseline during the lob's flight.
Score one for the lob deep, one more if the hitter is back on the baseline before it lands.
Six balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder follows the deep ball with a short ball that the hitter must reach from the recovered position.
coaching_points: Open the face and lift from the legs; the lob must peak above fence height to be deep.
Aim the lob cross-court and deep; a short lob is an overhead for them.
Recover during the flight, not after the bounce: the lob's height is your recovery time.
Recover to a metre inside the baseline, ready to attack the short reply.
progressions: Feeder follows every lob with a short ball.
Lobs must land within two metres of the far baseline.
Feeder stands at the net and the lob must clear an overhead attempt.
regressions: Feeder feeds at three-quarter pace.
Widen the lob target to anywhere past the far service line.
Feeder waits after the lob before the next feed.

name: First-Step Anticipation: Read the Racket Face
summary: Trains the reader to call the direction of a match-pace ball from the hitter's shoulders and racket face before it leaves the strings.
setup: One player on each baseline. The reader stands on the near centre mark between two cones placed a metre either side. The hitter on the far baseline has the basket and hits from a self-drop to either corner of the near court. No rally: one ball at a time.
instructions: Hitter drops and hits a ball to either near corner, at match pace.
Reader calls 'left' or 'right' before the ball leaves the strings, reading the hitter's shoulders and racket face, then moves and returns the ball deep.
Score one for a correct early call, one for the return in.
Ten balls, then swap roles.
Second round: the hitter tries to disguise, and a late call still counts if the return goes in.
coaching_points: Read the racket face and the front shoulder in the last half metre before contact; the ball's flight is too late.
Split as the racket comes forward so the landing is at contact.
Commit to the first step on the read; a wrong step corrected early beats a late right one.
Recover to the centre mark before the next self-drop.
progressions: Hitter adds the short ball as a third option.
Reader must call before the hitter's backswing is complete.
Play the point out after the return.
regressions: Hitter hits at three-quarter pace.
Hitter calls the direction out loud for the first five balls.
Reader moves after contact but still calls the direction.

name: Crossover Sprint to the Wide Feed
summary: Explosive crossover first steps to balls fed well beyond the sideline, with the next feed timed off the recovery.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, driving balls beyond the near singles sideline. Hitter starts on a throwdown on the near baseline a metre to the backhand side of the centre mark. A cone two metres outside the singles sideline, level with the baseline, marks where the wide ball is met. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline on the backhand side.
instructions: Feeder drives a ball wide to the cone.
Hitter explodes off the throwdown with a crossover first step, sprints to the ball, hits it cross-court and deep, and recovers to the throwdown.
Feeder feeds the next ball the moment the hitter's foot touches the throwdown.
Six balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder alternates the wide ball with a ball to the throwdown that must be hit without moving.
coaching_points: First step is a crossover: the inside foot crosses in front and the hips turn towards the ball.
Keep the racket back during the sprint so the last step and the swing are one motion.
Contact in front even at full stretch; hit up and cross-court to buy time.
Recover with crossovers first, side steps only for the last two metres.
progressions: Move the cone another metre wider.
Feeder feeds before the hitter reaches the throwdown.
The recovery ball must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline.
regressions: Move the cone onto the singles sideline.
Feeder waits until the hitter is still on the throwdown.
Feeder feeds at three-quarter pace.

name: Deceleration Control: Stop in the Throwdown Box
summary: Sprint to a one-metre throwdown square, come to a full balanced stop inside it, and only then hit, to train braking before contact.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket, tossing underarm. Hitter on the near baseline at the centre mark. A square of four throwdowns, one metre by one metre, two metres to the forehand side of the centre mark, marks where the hitter must come to a complete stop before hitting. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses a ball to bounce beside the throwdown square.
Hitter sprints to the square, decelerates to a complete stop inside it with a wide base, and only then hits the ball over the net.
Score one for a stop fully inside the square, one for the ball in.
Eight balls, then rotate.
Second round: the square moves to the backhand side.
coaching_points: Decelerate with the last two steps, feet wide and hips low; the stop is a brake, not a collapse.
Land the outside foot on the far edge of the square and let the inside foot settle.
Hit from the stopped base with the weight moving forward, not sideways.
Recover only after the ball has left the strings.
progressions: Shrink the square to half a metre.
Feeder tosses so the ball arrives a beat earlier and the stop must be faster.
Move the square three metres from the centre mark.
regressions: Widen the square to two metres.
Feeder waits until the hitter has stopped before tossing.
Move the square one metre from the centre mark.

name: Three Cross-Court Before You Change
summary: Points where each player must hit three cross-court balls before changing direction, teaching patience and the moment to go down the line.
setup: One player on each baseline, both starting on the deuce side. Basket at the net post. Points are played on the singles court with one rule: each player must hit three cross-court balls before they are allowed to change direction down the line.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed cross-court, alternating who starts.
Each player counts their own cross-court balls; a down-the-line ball before the third cross-court loses the point.
After three cross-court balls a player may change direction whenever they choose; the point then plays out normally.
First to eleven, then switch to the ad side.
Second game: the count is two.
coaching_points: Cross-court is the high-percentage ball: over the low part of the net, into the long diagonal.
Change direction off a ball you are set for, inside the baseline, not off a ball that has pushed you back.
After changing direction, recover past the centre; the reply comes back cross-court fast.
Count out loud for the first game so the habit sticks.
progressions: Only balls landing past the service line count towards the three.
The change of direction must land in a two-metre lane along the sideline.
Start points from a serve.
regressions: Cooperate through the first three balls, then the point goes live.
The count is one.
Play from the service lines.

name: Deep Middle Neutral Ball
summary: A cooperative rally into a deep-middle box at each end, teaching the ball that resets a point and gives the opponent no angle.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. A throwdown line two metres inside each baseline, with throwdowns two metres either side of the centre mark on it, marks a deep-middle box at each end. Basket at the net post.
instructions: Rally cooperatively; every ball must land in the partner's deep-middle box.
A ball outside the box ends the rally; count consecutive box balls.
A rally of ten banks a point; first to three points.
Second round: play the point out after ten box balls; the point can be won only by a ball deliberately played outside the box, an angle or a short ball.
Third round: box balls must also clear the net by two racket lengths.
coaching_points: Aim high over the middle strap and let the ball drop deep; the middle gives your opponent no angle.
Use the deep middle ball when you are off balance or behind the baseline; it resets the point.
Recover to the centre mark: a middle ball comes back down the middle.
Heavy, not hard: the ball should bounce up above the partner's waist.
progressions: Shrink the box to two metres wide.
Play points where only the deep middle ball may be hit until someone is pulled inside the service line.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Widen the box to the whole area past the service line.
Play from the service lines.
Use an orange ball.

name: Serve, Then First Ball Cross-Court
summary: Points from a serve where the server's first groundstroke must go cross-court, building the safest start to a point.
setup: One player each side behind the baselines on the singles court, playing points from a serve. Basket beside the server. One rule: the server's first ball after the serve must go cross-court, or the point is lost.
instructions: Server serves; the returner returns anywhere.
The server's next ball must go cross-court from wherever it is played; after that the point is open.
Play to seven points, then swap server.
Second game: the returner's first ball, the return, must also go cross-court.
Third game: the first ball must go cross-court and deep past the service line.
coaching_points: Land from the serve and split; the cross-court first ball starts with the feet, not the racket.
Cross-court off the return is the safe high-percentage start; it gives the returner nothing to attack.
If the return is short, still go cross-court but take it early and hit through it.
Recover after the first ball to the side you hit from, ready for the cross-court reply.
progressions: The first ball must land in a two-metre box in the far cross-court corner.
Second serves only, no first serves.
The first ball must be hit from inside the baseline.
regressions: Serve from the service line.
Cooperate for the serve, return and first ball, then play the point out.
The first ball may go cross-court or down the middle.

name: Height Change: Loop, Then Drive
summary: A cooperative rally where one player loops high and heavy and the other drives flat, so both learn to change and handle height.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. A cooperative rally in which one player hits every ball as a high looping topspin ball and the other answers every ball with a flat drive. Singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Player A starts with a high loop; B answers with a flat drive; A loops again, B drives again, for the whole rally.
Rally to twelve balls, then swap roles without stopping if possible.
A loop that lands short of the service line, or a drive that clears the net by more than a racket length, ends the rally.
Keep a tally of the longest rally in each role.
Second round: each player alternates their own loop and drive, ball by ball.
coaching_points: Loop: swing steeply low to high with a fast racket head; the ball peaks above fence height.
Drive: contact out in front, swing through the ball and finish forward at shoulder height.
Take the loop early or let it drop; do not hit it at shoulder height on the way up.
Change the height, not the swing speed: both balls are hit with a full swing.
progressions: Loops must land past a throwdown line two metres inside the baseline.
Play the point out after eight balls; a change of height wins the point if the partner misses.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Loop only until ten in a row, then add the drive.
Play from the service lines.
Use an orange ball.

name: Doubles Basics: Serve, Cross-Court, Call the Poach
summary: Doubles points with a cross-court return rule and a called poach, so the four positions learn their first jobs.
setup: Four players in doubles formation: server behind the near baseline on the deuce side, server's partner at the near net on the ad side, returner behind the far baseline on the deuce side, returner's partner on the far service line on the ad side. Basket beside the server.
instructions: Server serves; the returner must return cross-court.
Server's partner may poach the return only if they called 'go' to the server before the serve; otherwise they hold.
Play the point out as normal doubles.
Four points, then rotate all four positions clockwise.
Second round: the returner may go down the line if the net player has called 'go' twice in a row.
coaching_points: Returner: cross-court and low over the net; the net player is waiting for anything high.
Net player: if you called 'go', move as the returner makes contact, diagonally forward.
Server: after calling 'go' with your partner, serve down the T so the cross-court return is easier to poach.
Returner's partner: split as the server makes contact and watch the net player, not the ball.
progressions: Net player must poach at least once every four points.
Returner may go down the line at any time.
Server must serve and volley when 'go' is called.
regressions: No poaching: the net player holds and the point is played cross-court.
Server serves from the service line.
Returner hand-feeds the return instead of returning a serve.

name: Target the Backhand Points
summary: Points where every ball must land in the opponent's backhand half, building the habit of attacking the weaker side.
setup: One player on each baseline. Cones on each baseline and service line at the centre line split each court into a forehand half and a backhand half; for right-handers the backhand half is the left half looking at the net. Basket at the net post. Points on the singles court with one rule: every ball must land in the opponent's backhand half.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed, alternating who starts.
A ball landing in the opponent's forehand half loses the point.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: one ball per point may go to the forehand half, chosen by the hitter.
Third game: the rule applies only after the fourth ball.
coaching_points: Aim a metre inside the centre line, not at the sideline; the backhand half is big.
Use the cross-court backhand and the inside-out forehand: both go to the backhand half naturally.
Recover to the backhand side of the centre mark; that is where the reply is coming from.
When the opponent runs around to hit a forehand, the forehand half is open: remember it for the second game.
progressions: Balls must land in the backhand half and past the service line.
Play from a serve; the serve must also go to the backhand.
Points can be won only with a ball to the forehand half after four to the backhand.
regressions: Cooperate for four balls before the point goes live.
Balls may land anywhere in the backhand half or down the middle.
Play from the service lines.

name: Backhand Cross-Court Until Short, Then Inside-Out Forehand
summary: A backhand cross-court rally that goes live the moment a ball lands short, with the run-around inside-out forehand as the attacking answer.
setup: One player on each baseline, both on the ad side, so the rally is backhand cross-court for right-handers. Throwdowns along each service line mark the short zone. Basket at the net post. Singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Rally backhand cross-court cooperatively.
The moment a ball lands short, inside the service line, the receiver runs around it and hits an inside-out forehand to the opponent's backhand corner, and the point is live.
Play the point out; a point won after the inside-out forehand scores two, any other point one.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: the inside-out forehand must also be followed to the net.
coaching_points: Read the short ball as it leaves the racket and move around it early; three quick steps left.
Inside-out to the backhand corner keeps the pattern: their weakest reply from their weakest side.
After the inside-out ball, recover a step to the left of centre; the reply is coming cross-court to your forehand.
If the short ball is very short, go inside-in down the line instead and follow it in.
progressions: The inside-out forehand must land in a two-metre corner box.
Start points from a serve into the backhand.
Any ball landing within two metres behind the service line also counts as short.
regressions: Cooperate through the inside-out ball, then the point goes live.
The short ball may be attacked with any shot.
Widen the short zone with throwdowns two metres behind the service line.

name: Approach Decision: Line or Middle by Position
summary: Teaches the approach-shot rule of thumb, down the line from the sides and deep middle from the centre, with a passing shot to volley afterwards.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding short balls with the racket to the left, centre or right of the near court. Player on the near baseline at the centre mark. Three cones on the near service line, left, centre and right, mark the three landing areas; a cone in each far corner and one on the far centre mark show the approach targets. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds a short ball to one of the three cones.
Player approaches with the rule: from the sides, approach down the line; from the centre, approach deep down the middle.
Feeder feeds a passing shot and the player volleys it.
Score one for the approach to the right target, one for the volley in; six sequences, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder tries a lob instead of a pass every third ball.
coaching_points: Down the line from the sides: the shortest distance to the net position and the smallest gap to cover.
Deep middle from the centre: it takes away the angles for the pass.
Follow the approach on the same side of the centre as the ball; the volley position is not the middle.
Split as the feeder makes contact with the passing shot.
progressions: Approaches must land in two-metre target boxes.
Feeder feeds the passing shot sooner.
Play the point out after the volley with the feeder.
regressions: Feeder calls 'line' or 'middle' with each feed.
Remove the passing shot: approach and stop.
Feeder tosses the short ball underarm.

name: Doubles: Serve and Volley with the Poach Signal
summary: Doubles points where the server follows every serve in and the net player signals a poach or a stay before each point.
setup: Four players in doubles formation: server behind the near baseline on the deuce side, server's partner at the near net on the ad side, returner behind the far baseline on the deuce side, returner's partner on the far service line on the ad side. Basket beside the server. Before each point the net player signals behind their back: open hand for poach, fist for stay.
instructions: Net player signals; the server serves and follows the serve to the net.
On a poach signal, the net player crosses as the returner makes contact and the server covers the vacated side.
Play the point out.
Four points, then rotate all four positions clockwise.
Second round: the returning pair may signal a down-the-line return or a lob in the same way.
coaching_points: Server: first volley deep to the returner's feet, then close.
Net player on a poach: move diagonally forward on contact and finish the volley at the far net player's feet.
Server on a poach: cross behind your partner as soon as they move; the switch is automatic.
Returning pair: a low cross-court return is the answer to everything here; a high one gets poached.
progressions: Net player must poach at least every second point.
Returner may lob at any time.
Server serves second serves only and must still come in.
regressions: Server stays back; only the net player poaches.
Returner returns cross-court only, no lobs or lines.
Serve from the service line.

name: Rally Length Discipline: Win Only After Ball Six
summary: Points that only count from the sixth ball, so the early balls are used to build position rather than to go for winners.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. Points on the singles court from an underarm feed, with one rule: a point ended before the sixth ball, by a winner or an error, is replayed.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed, alternating who starts.
Count balls out loud; any point that ends before ball six is replayed, whoever ended it.
From ball six the point is live and counts.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: the count starts at eight.
coaching_points: The first five balls are for position, not winners: deep, cross-court, high margin.
Use the early balls to move the opponent, so ball six starts from an advantage.
Recover to the right spot after every ball; the point is longer than you want it to be.
When ball six arrives, attack only what is short; a deep ball is still a rally ball.
progressions: The count starts at ten.
Start from a serve; the serve counts as ball one.
An error before ball six loses the point outright.
regressions: The count starts at four.
Cooperate through the first five balls and go live on ball six.
Play from the service lines.

name: Change of Pace: The Slow Ball Trap
summary: A rally in which either player may throw in a slow high ball at any time, and the receiver must recognise it and attack.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Throwdown lines two metres inside each baseline mark the deep zones. Basket at the net post. A cooperative rally at rally pace in which either player may, at any time, play a slow high ball; the point is live from that ball.
instructions: Rally cooperatively at rally pace, deep into the throwdown zones.
At any time either player may play a slow, high, loopy ball; the receiver must attack it, taking it early, and the point is live.
The attacker scores two for winning the point, the slow-ball player one.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: the slow ball must be answered with an approach and a finish at the net.
coaching_points: Recognise the slow ball early: move in and take it at the top of the bounce or on the rise, never let it drop.
Attack with margin: deep to a corner, not a winner on the line.
After attacking, move forward a metre; the reply will be short or a lob.
If the slow ball is very deep, take it in the air with a swinging volley or reset with a slow ball of your own.
progressions: The attack must land in a two-metre corner box.
Start points from a serve.
The slow-ball player may follow it to the net.
regressions: Cooperate through the attack, then the point goes live.
The slow ball must be announced as it is hit.
Widen the deep zones to everything past the service line.

name: Half-Court Live: Deep or Lose
summary: Half-court points where any ball landing short of a deep-zone line loses immediately, making depth the whole game.
setup: Both players on the same half of the court lengthways, one each side of the net. Cones on each baseline and service line at the centre line mark the boundary. A throwdown line two metres inside each baseline across the half marks the deep zone. Basket at the net post.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed, alternating who starts.
Every ball must land past the throwdown line; a ball that lands short loses the point immediately.
First to eleven, then play the other half.
Second game: one ball per point may land between the service line and the throwdown line.
Third game: the deep rule applies only to the first four balls.
coaching_points: Height is depth: aim two racket lengths over the net.
Heavy topspin lets you hit deep with margin; a flat ball must be perfect to be deep.
Take the ball early when it lands short so you can still hit deep from inside the baseline.
Recover behind the baseline; the deep ball at you is coming back deep.
progressions: Move the throwdown line to one metre inside the baseline.
Start points from a serve.
A ball into the deep zone from inside the baseline scores double.
regressions: Move the throwdown line to the service line.
Cooperate for four balls before the point goes live.
Allow one short ball per point.

name: Doubles Formation: I-Formation Serve
summary: Introduces the I-formation, with the net player crouched on the centre line and a signalled move as the return is struck.
setup: Four players in doubles formation, but the serving pair use the I-formation: server behind the near baseline on the centre mark, server's partner crouched at the near net on the centre line. Returner behind the far baseline on the deuce side, returner's partner on the far service line on the ad side. Basket beside the server. Before each point the net player signals which side they will move to.
instructions: Net player signals left or right behind their back; the server serves down the T.
As the returner makes contact, the net player moves to the signalled side and the server covers the other side.
Play the point out.
Four points, then rotate all four positions.
Second round: the returner may lob or go down the line; the serving pair must still commit to the signal.
coaching_points: Net player: stay crouched and still until the returner's racket meets the ball, then move.
Server: the serve goes down the T so the returner has no angle past the net player.
Server: the covered side is the whole other half; move as your partner moves.
Returner: return low down the middle or lob; the sidelines are guarded by the moving net player.
progressions: The net player may fake one way and go the other.
Server serves and volleys behind the I-formation.
Returner must return within a metre of the sideline to score.
regressions: Net player announces the side out loud before the serve.
Returner must return down the middle.
Serve from the service line.

name: Break Point Plans: Say It, Then Serve It
summary: Every point starts at 30-40 and the server must state the serve, first ball and recovery plan out loud before executing it.
setup: Server behind the near baseline with the basket, returner behind the far baseline, on the singles court. Every point starts at 30-40 on the server's serve. Nothing else on court.
instructions: Before each point, the server says the plan out loud: serve target, first ball, and where they will recover.
Server serves and both play the point out.
Score two for the server if the point is won using the stated plan, one if won another way; the returner scores one for any point won.
Ten points, then swap roles.
Second round: the returner also states a return plan, quietly enough that the server cannot hear it.
coaching_points: A break point plan is a percentage plan: the highest first-serve percentage target, then cross-court.
Say the recovery spot too; the plan is finished only when your feet are in position.
If the first serve misses, the second-serve plan is body serve, then deep middle.
Slow the routine down at 30-40: two bounces more than usual.
progressions: Start points at deuce and ad-out as well.
The server must use a different plan every point.
Points are played as a full game from 30-40.
regressions: Start points at 15-all.
The server states the serve target only.
Serve from the service line.

name: Return Position Chess: Move Before the Toss
summary: The returner changes starting position before every point to bait a serve, then scores double when the serve goes where the position invited it.
setup: Server behind the near baseline with the basket, returner behind the far baseline, singles court. The returner changes starting position before every point: a metre inside the baseline, two metres behind it, or a metre towards the alley. Nothing else on court.
instructions: Before each point the returner picks a new starting position and stands in it early, so the server sees it.
Server serves and both play the point out.
The returner scores two if the point is won and the serve went where the position invited it, for example wide when standing inside; the server scores one for any point won.
Ten points, then swap roles.
Second round: the returner moves during the toss instead of before it.
coaching_points: Your position is a message: standing inside says 'I will attack the second serve', standing wide says 'serve down the T'.
Move early and then be still; a moving returner at contact is late.
Decide the return before the serve based on the position you chose: block from inside, drive from deep.
After the return, recover to the centre mark; the position trick is over once the ball is in play.
progressions: The returner must change position on every point and never repeat one.
Second serves only, with the returner inside the baseline on every point.
The server may serve to either box.
regressions: Two positions only: normal and inside.
The server tells the returner where the serve is going.
Serve from the service line.

name: Run-Around Forehand or Neutral Backhand: Decide by Ball Height
summary: Three feed heights into the backhand corner, each with a prescribed answer, so the run-around decision is made from the ball's height.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket to the near backhand corner at three heights: low skidding, waist height, and high looping. Player on the near baseline at the centre mark. A two-metre cone box in the far backhand corner and a cone on the far centre mark show the two targets. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds to the backhand corner at one of the three heights.

Player applies the rule: high ball, run around and hit an inside-out forehand into the cone box; waist height, backhand cross-court into the box; low ball, backhand slice deep down the middle to the centre cone.
Score two for the right shot into the right target, one for the right shot anywhere in, zero for the wrong shot.
Nine balls, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder adds pace so the decision must be faster.
coaching_points: Decide by the height as the ball leaves the feeder's racket; a late decision leaves you between two shots.
High ball: get around it early and take it at shoulder height with the inside-out forehand.
Waist height: the backhand drive is the reliable option; do not run around a ball you can hit well.
Low ball: slice deep and reset; nobody attacks a low skidding ball.
progressions: Feeder mixes in the forehand corner with the same three heights.
Shrink the cone box to one metre.
Play the point out with the feeder after the reply.
regressions: Feeder calls the height before feeding.
Two heights only: high and low.
Widen the targets to the whole far half.

name: Sneak Attack: Approach off the Deep Ball
summary: Approaching off a deep ball taken on the rise, rather than waiting for a short one, so the surprise comes from timing.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Throwdown lines two metres inside each baseline mark the deep zone. Basket at the net post. A cooperative deep rally in which the approach is made off a deep ball, taken on the rise, rather than off a short one.
instructions: Rally cooperatively, deep into the throwdown zones.
At any time either player may take a deep ball on the rise from inside the baseline and follow it to the net; the point is live from that ball.
The approacher scores two for winning the point, the baseliner one.
First to eleven, then change ends.
Second game: the approach must be a backhand slice.
coaching_points: Take the ball on the rise a metre inside the baseline; the surprise is the timing, not the pace.
Approach down the line and deep; the ball must not sit up.
Move forward through the shot; the split at the service line comes as the opponent makes contact.
First volley deep, second volley to the open court.
progressions: The approach must land past the throwdown line.
Start points from a serve; the server may approach off the return.
The baseliner may lob at any time.
regressions: Cooperate through the approach and first volley, then the point goes live.
The approach may be made off any ball.
Widen the deep zones to everything past the service line.

name: Two-on-One: The One Attacks
summary: One attacker tries to win points against two cooperative defenders who cover the whole court, forcing patience and depth before the finish.
setup: One attacker on the near baseline at the centre mark. Two defenders on the far baseline, one on each half, with the basket between them at the centre. The attacker plays the whole singles court; the defenders each cover their own half.
instructions: A defender starts the point with a deep feed.
The attacker tries to win the point against both defenders, who return everything cooperatively but deep and may hit winners only off short balls.
Attacker scores two for a winner or forced error; defenders score one for a point won.
Eight points, then rotate: attacker to left defender, left defender to right defender, right defender to attacker.
Second round: the attacker must finish every point at the net.
coaching_points: Against two players the sidelines are covered; win through the middle and with depth, then angle when they are pulled in.
Change height and pace to create the short ball; two defenders do not miss the easy one.
Take the short ball early and approach behind it; the finish comes at the net, not from the baseline.
Recover to the centre mark every time; two defenders can hit either corner.
progressions: Defenders may attack any ball.
Attacker must win within six balls.
Defenders may lob at any time.
regressions: Defenders hit at three-quarter pace.
Defenders may not hit winners at all.
Attacker scores for any point won, not only winners.

name: Doubles: Australian Formation
summary: The serving pair line up on the same side to take away the cross-court return, and switch as the serve is struck.
setup: Four players in doubles formation, serving pair in the Australian formation: server behind the near baseline close to the centre mark on the deuce side, server's partner at the near net on the same deuce side. Returner behind the far baseline on the deuce side, returner's partner on the far service line on the ad side. Basket beside the server. Before each point the net player signals stay or poach.
instructions: Server serves; with the net player on the server's own side, the cross-court return is covered and the returner must go down the line or lob.
Server moves to the open ad side after serving; the net player poaches or holds according to the signal.
Play the point out.
Four points, then rotate all four positions.
Second round: use the formation on the ad side as well.
coaching_points: Server: serve down the T or into the body so the down-the-line return is hard to hit.
Server: land and move immediately to the open side; the return is coming there.
Net player: cover the middle and be ready for the lob over you; the down-the-line return is the server's ball.
Returner: the down-the-line return must be low and deep; a short one is a volley for the net player.
progressions: The net player may poach the down-the-line return.
Server must serve and volley from the Australian formation.
Returner must return down the line on every point.
regressions: Net player announces stay or poach out loud.
Returner may return anywhere; the serving pair simply practise the switch.
Serve from the service line.

name: Drop Shot and Lob Combinations: Touch Points
summary: Points where drop shots and lobs score double, so touch becomes a tactic rather than an afterthought.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. Points on the singles court from an underarm feed, with drop shots and lobs scored double.
instructions: Start each point with an underarm feed, alternating who starts.
Play the point out; a point won with a drop shot, a lob, or a drop shot followed by a lob scores two, any other point one.
First to fifteen, then change ends.
Second game: the point can only be won with a drop shot or a lob; everything else is replayed.
Third game: normal scoring but each player must play at least one drop shot and one lob per point.
coaching_points: Drop shot off a short ball only, from inside the baseline, with the same take-back as the drive.
After the drop shot, move in: the reply is a drop shot or a lob, and both are answered from the service line.
Lob when the opponent is at the net and leaning forward; aim over the backhand shoulder, deep.
Disguise: the opponent should read the drop shot from the bounce, not from the swing.
progressions: Drop shots must be played from behind the service line.
Lobs must land within two metres of the baseline.
Start points from a serve.
regressions: Drop shots and lobs score normally but must be attempted at least once per point.
Cooperate for four balls before the point goes live.
Play from the service lines.

name: Tiebreak from 4-4: Rally Tolerance Under Score Pressure
summary: Repeated tiebreaks that start at 4-4, so every point is played at the score where matches are decided.
setup: One player each side behind the baselines, singles court, basket beside the server. Every set of points is a tiebreak that starts at 4-4, with normal serving order and changing ends at the usual moments.
instructions: Play a tiebreak from 4-4 to seven, win by two.
The winner of each tiebreak notes how many points ended with an unforced error inside six balls.
Play four tiebreaks, alternating who serves first.
Fifth tiebreak from 5-5.
Last tiebreak: the loser of each point must say what they would do differently before the next serve.
coaching_points: At 4-4 the first two serves decide the tiebreak: highest-percentage serve, first ball cross-court.
Under pressure, add a metre of margin to every target; the opponent misses first if you do not.
Same routine every point: towel, bounce, breathe; the score does not change the routine.
On match point against you, play the pattern that has been working, not a hero shot.
progressions: Start every tiebreak at 5-5.
Second serves only, no first serves.
The loser of the previous tiebreak serves first at 4-5.
regressions: Start tiebreaks at 3-3.
Tiebreaks to five instead of seven.
Serve from a metre inside the baseline.

name: Call Your Pattern Before the Point
summary: Both players announce their two-shot pattern before every point and score double for winning it that way, even though the opponent heard.
setup: One player each side behind the baselines, singles court, basket beside the server. Before each point both players announce, out loud to each other, the two-shot pattern they intend to play first; the opponent hearing it is part of the drill.
instructions: Before each point, each player announces their first two-shot pattern out loud, for example 'serve wide, forehand to the open court' or 'return deep middle, then attack the short ball'.
Play the point out from a serve.
Score two if the point is won using the announced pattern, one if won another way.
Ten points, then swap server.
Second round: patterns must be three shots long.
coaching_points: A pattern is a plan for the first two balls only; after that, play what you see.
Announcing the pattern to the opponent is the point: a good pattern works even when it is known.
If the first ball of the pattern is missed, the pattern is over; reset to cross-court and deep.
Choose patterns that start with your strength and end on their weakness.
progressions: Patterns must be three shots long.
Players whisper the pattern to a third player who scores it, so the opponent does not know.
The same pattern may not be used twice in a row.
regressions: Patterns are one shot long: the serve target or the return target.
Cooperate through the pattern, then the point goes live.
Serve from the service line.

name: Dynamic Line Warm-Up: Skips, Carioca, Lunges
summary: A no-ball movement warm-up between two cones that raises the heart rate and opens the hips and shoulders before hitting.
setup: Two cones fifteen metres apart along the back fence or in the space behind a baseline. Players line up at the first cone, an arm's length apart, and move to the second cone and back on each exercise. No balls needed.
instructions: Jog to the far cone and back, then side-shuffle there and back.
High knees there, heel flicks back.
Carioca, crossover steps, there and back, facing the same way both times.
Walking lunges there, then walking lunges with a trunk rotation back.
Finish with three short accelerations from a split step, ten metres each.
coaching_points: Keep every movement light on the balls of the feet.
Lunges: front knee over the ankle, back knee to the ground, chest up.
Carioca: hips loose, shoulders facing forward, arms relaxed.
Accelerations: the first step is small and quick, not a leap.
progressions: Add a second set of the movement exercises at a faster tempo.
Increase the cone distance to twenty metres.
Add a ball toss and catch with a partner during the jog.
regressions: Walk every exercise the first time through.
Shorten the cone distance to ten metres.
Replace the carioca with side shuffles.

name: Band Shoulder Activation
summary: A five-minute resistance band routine that wakes up the rotator cuff and shoulder blades before serving and overheads.
setup: Each player with a light resistance band, standing beside the court or behind the baseline with an arm's length of space. Bands looped around a fence post for the serving action, held in both hands for the pull-aparts.
instructions: Band pull-aparts: hold the band at shoulder height, pull the hands apart until the band touches the chest, ten times.
External rotations: elbow tucked at the side, forearm across the body, rotate out against the band, ten each arm.
Overhead press with the band under the front foot, ten times.
Serving action against the band looped on the fence: slow trophy position to contact, eight times.
Finish with ten arm circles each way with no band.
coaching_points: Shoulder blades down and back before every pull; the band is for the small muscles, not the arms.
Slow on the way back: two seconds out, three seconds back.
External rotations: the elbow stays glued to the side.
Breathe out on the effort.
progressions: Use a medium band instead of a light one.
Two sets of everything.
Add a slow backhand action against the band.
regressions: Use the lightest band, or none and just the arm movements.
Five repetitions instead of ten.
Skip the overhead press.

name: Agility Ladder Foot Patterns
summary: Four ladder patterns run in a queue to wake up the feet, finishing with a split step and a sprint.
setup: Agility ladder laid flat behind the baseline or beside the court. Players queue at one end, an arm's length apart, and jog back down the outside after each run.
instructions: Two feet in every box, forwards.
In-in-out-out: both feet in, then both feet out to the sides, moving forward.
Lateral: side-on, both feet in every box, then the other way.
Icky shuffle: in, in, out, moving diagonally through the ladder.
Finish with one run at full speed with any pattern, then a split step and a sprint to the net.
coaching_points: Eyes ahead, not on the ladder; the feet learn the pattern faster than the eyes.
Small quick steps, arms pumping.
Stay low with the knees bent through the lateral patterns.
Land the last step outside the ladder into a split step.
progressions: Add a ball toss and catch from a partner during the run.
Two runs of each pattern.
Time the runs and try to beat the previous time.
regressions: Walk each pattern once before running it.
Two patterns only: two feet in, and lateral.
Remove the sprint at the end.

name: Partner Ball Toss Reactions
summary: A no-racket catching warm-up in pairs that gets the eyes, hands and split step working before the first ball is hit.
setup: Pairs facing each other three metres apart beside the court, one ball each. No rackets.
instructions: Both players toss their ball underarm to the partner at the same time and catch the incoming one; twenty catches.
One player tosses to either side; the partner shuffles and catches, then tosses back; ten each.
Toss high; the partner turns sideways and catches above the head, then throws it back overarm; ten each.
Toss to the feet; the partner lunges and catches low; ten each.
Finish with a reaction round: the tosser fakes one way and tosses the other.
coaching_points: Catch with the hands in front of the body, eyes on the ball all the way into the hands.
Split step as the partner's arm starts to move.
Turn sideways for the high catch and point at the ball with the other hand.
Low catch: bend from the knees, chest up.
progressions: Increase the distance to five metres.
Use two balls at once in the side-to-side round.
Catch with one hand only.
regressions: Reduce the distance to two metres.
Toss straight to the hands for every round.
Use a red ball.

name: Net to Baseline Warm-Up Ladder: Two Minutes a Station
summary: A hitting warm-up that walks back from volleys at the net to full baseline rallies in four timed stations.
setup: Two players on the singles court with a basket at the net post. Four stations, two minutes each: both at the net volleying, both inside the service lines rallying mini tennis, both at three-quarter court, both on the baselines.
instructions: Volley-volley across the net for two minutes, cooperative, no bounce.
Step back to the service lines and rally gently inside the service boxes for two minutes.
Step back to three-quarter court and rally cross-court at half pace for two minutes.
Baselines: rally down the middle for two minutes, building to rally pace.
Finish with one minute where each player serves five easy serves into each box.
coaching_points: Start at half pace and build; the warm-up is finished when the body says so, not the clock.
Move the feet on every ball from the first volley; a lazy warm-up becomes a lazy session.
Aim for the partner's hip so the rally keeps going.
On the baselines, add topspin before adding pace.
progressions: Shorten each station to ninety seconds and add a fifth: overheads off a hand-fed lob.
Rally cross-court on both diagonals at the three-quarter station.
Serve and return points to finish instead of serving alone.
regressions: Skip the baseline station and finish at three-quarter court.
Use an orange ball at the first two stations.
Three minutes per station at the same pace throughout.

name: Toss, Volley, Lob: Net Warm-Up
summary: A short hand-fed net warm-up of easy volleys, low volleys and half-pace overheads before net drills.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, tossing underarm. Player at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side. Extra players queue behind the player.
instructions: Feeder tosses five easy forehand volleys, then five backhand volleys, hit back gently to the feeder.
Feeder tosses five low volleys at the feet.
Feeder lobs five easy balls for overheads hit at half pace into the far court.
Rotate the player.
Last round: the feeder mixes volleys and lobs without warning.
coaching_points: Rackets up and in front from the first ball.
Half pace on the overheads; the shoulder is warming up, not being tested.
Step in on every volley, step back to ready between balls.
Turn sideways early on the lobs.
progressions: Feeder hits the feeds with a racket from the far baseline.
Add five swinging volleys off a floating ball.
Player must volley to alternate sides.
regressions: Replace the overheads with five more volleys.
Feeder tosses from the same side of the net.
Use an orange ball.

name: Rally Speed Ladder: 50, 70, 90 Percent
summary: A baseline warm-up rally that steps up through three called paces so the body reaches match speed gradually.
setup: One player on each baseline at the centre mark, basket at the net post. The rally is cooperative down the middle and the pace is set by a called percentage.
instructions: Rally at fifty percent pace for two minutes, high over the net, deep.
Call 'seventy' and rally at seventy percent for two minutes, adding topspin.
Call 'ninety' and rally for two minutes at near match pace, still cooperative.
Finish with one minute of live points from a hand-feed.
Any ball the partner cannot keep in the rally is too hard for that percentage: drop back a step.
coaching_points: Pace comes from the legs and the racket-head speed, not from swinging harder with the arm.
Keep the same net clearance at every percentage; only the spin and racket speed change.
Recover to the centre mark after every ball, even at fifty percent.
Breathe out on contact at ninety percent.
progressions: Add a fourth step: one hundred percent for one minute.
Rally cross-court instead of down the middle.
Live points for two minutes instead of one.
regressions: Two steps only: fifty and seventy.
Rally from the service lines for the first step.
Use a green ball.

name: Doubles Warm-Up Rotation: Two Minutes at Each Station
summary: Four players warm up on one court with timed net-and-baseline stations, rotating roles and halves every two minutes.
setup: Four players on one court, one pair each side of the net. Station one: one player at the net and one on the baseline on each side, so the net players volley against the opposite baseliner down their own half. Basket at the net post. Every two minutes the pairs rotate: net player to baseline, baseline player to net, then swap halves.
instructions: Net players volley against the opposite baseliners, cooperatively, down each half for two minutes.
Rotate: the baseliners come to the net and the net players go back.
Rotate again and switch halves so everyone has volleyed on the deuce and ad sides.
Fourth station: all four on the baselines, rallying cross-court in two pairs.
Finish with each player hitting five overheads off a hand-fed lob from their partner.
coaching_points: Baseliners: hit at the net player's hip so they can volley without moving much.
Net players: deep volleys, not angles; the baseliner needs the ball back.
Rotate quickly; the two minutes includes the walk.
Cross-court rallies: stay in your half and let the other pair have theirs.
progressions: Ninety seconds per station.
Net players must volley to alternate sides of the baseliner.
Finish with two minutes of doubles points instead of overheads.
regressions: Three minutes per station.
Skip the overheads and finish after the fourth station.
Use a green ball.

name: Walk Down and Static Stretch Sequence
summary: Two slow laps and a fixed order of held stretches for the calves, hamstrings, hips and forearms to finish a session.
setup: Players walk two laps of the court perimeter, then stand in a loose circle beside the court with an arm's length of space each. No equipment; one player leads the sequence and counts the holds out loud.
instructions: Walk two laps of the court, arms swinging, breathing through the nose.
Calf stretch against the fence, thirty seconds each leg.
Hamstring stretch with the heel on the ground and toes up, thirty seconds each leg.
Hip flexor lunge stretch, thirty seconds each side, then a forearm stretch with the palm flat against the fence.
Finish with a thirty-second forward fold and three slow breaths.
coaching_points: Stretch to a gentle pull, never to pain; the muscles are warm and will give.
Breathe out as you settle into each stretch.
Hold still: bouncing tightens the muscle rather than lengthening it.
Keep the back straight in the hamstring stretch; hinge from the hips.
progressions: Hold each stretch for forty-five seconds.
Add a thoracic rotation stretch on the ground.
Add a second round of the calf and hamstring stretches.
regressions: Hold each stretch for twenty seconds.
Walk one lap instead of two.
Do the stretches seated against the fence.

name: Partner Stretch: Hamstrings and Hips
summary: Paired stretches for the hamstrings, groin and hips where one partner supports gently and counts while the other lets go.
setup: Pairs beside the court on a clean patch of ground, or a mat if there is one. One partner stretches while the other supports gently and counts; then they swap. No equipment.
instructions: Lying hamstring stretch: one partner lies on their back and lifts a straight leg; the other supports the heel and holds it at a gentle pull for thirty seconds, then the other leg.
Seated groin stretch: soles of the feet together, the partner presses the knees down lightly for thirty seconds.
Hip rotation: lying on the back, one knee across the body; the partner holds the shoulder down for thirty seconds each side.
Swap roles and repeat.
Finish with both partners standing and shaking out the legs for thirty seconds.
coaching_points: The supporting partner listens: the stretcher says 'there' and the pressure stops.
Breathe out as the leg goes up; the hamstring lets go on the out-breath.
Keep the other leg flat on the ground in the hamstring stretch.
Never push a stretch for a partner; hold, do not press.
progressions: Hold each stretch for forty-five seconds.
Add a contract-relax: push against the partner for five seconds, then relax deeper.
Add a lying quad stretch on the side.
regressions: Hold each stretch for twenty seconds.
Do the stretches alone against the fence instead of with a partner.
Skip the hip rotation.

name: Breathing and Slow Jog Cool-Down
summary: A slow jog that fades into a walk with counted breathing, bringing the heart rate down before stretching or leaving.
setup: Players jog slowly around the outside of the court in single file, an arm's length apart. No equipment.
instructions: Jog slowly for two minutes around the court, gradually slowing to a walk.
Walk one lap breathing in for four steps and out for six.
Stand still, hands on the head, and take five slow breaths.
Shake out the arms and legs for thirty seconds.
Finish with each player saying one thing they did well in the session.
coaching_points: Jog slower than feels natural; the heart rate should drop, not hold.
Breathe out longer than in; the long out-breath is what slows everything down.
Hands on the head opens the chest for the last breaths.
Keep talking to a minimum until the breathing is settled.
progressions: Jog for three minutes before slowing.
Add a lap of walking lunges before the breathing.
Breathe in for four steps and out for eight.
regressions: Walk instead of jogging.
One minute of jogging instead of two.
Skip the breathing count and simply walk a lap.

name: Band Recovery Circuit: Shoulders and Forearms
summary: A light resistance band circuit that flushes the shoulders and forearms after a serving-heavy session.
setup: Each player with a light resistance band, standing beside the court with an arm's length of space. The band is held in both hands for the pull-aparts and looped under the front foot for the rows and wrist curls.
instructions: Slow band pull-aparts, ten times, three seconds each way.
Band rows with the band under the front foot, ten times, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Wrist curls with the band under the foot, ten each way.
Forearm stretch with the palm against the fence, thirty seconds each arm.
Finish with slow arm circles, five each way, no band.
coaching_points: Slow and controlled; this is blood flow, not strength work.
Shoulder blades down and together on every row.
Wrist curls: only the wrist moves, the forearm stays on the thigh.
Breathe out on the pull.
progressions: Two rounds of the circuit.
Hold the forearm stretch for forty-five seconds.
Add an overhead band stretch, arms straight, ten seconds each side.
regressions: Five repetitions instead of ten.
Skip the rows and do the pull-aparts twice.
Do the stretches only, with no band.

name: King of the Court (Half Court)
summary: Challengers queue to take on the king down one half of the court; win the point and take the throne.
setup: One half of the court lengthways, singles sideline to centre line. The king stands on the far baseline of that half; challengers queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline. Basket at the net post. The challenger starts each point with a hand-feed.
instructions: Challenger starts the point with a hand-feed to the king.
Play the point inside the half; if the challenger wins, they become the king and the king joins the back of the queue.
If the king wins, the challenger goes to the back of the queue and the next challenger steps in.
Each player keeps a tally of points won as king; first to ten wins the game.
Second game: the king must win two points in a row against each challenger to keep the throne.
coaching_points: Challenger: hit the feed deep and get set; the king is waiting for a short one.
King: play the percentages; the next challenger is already coming.
Everyone: recover to the middle of the half after every ball.
Queue: track the point and be ready to step in as soon as it ends.
progressions: The point can be won only with a ball that lands past the service line.
Start points with a serve instead of a hand-feed.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Cooperate for three balls before the point goes live.
Use an orange ball.
Play across the service boxes only.

name: Around the World Rally
summary: A group rally where each player hits once and runs round the net post to the other queue, with the rally kept alive by the whole group.
setup: Two queues, one behind each baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. The first player in each queue plays the ball, then runs round the outside of the net post to join the back of the opposite queue while the rally continues.
instructions: The first player hits the ball over the net, then runs round the outside of the net post to the back of the other queue.
The next player in the opposite queue plays the ball and does the same, so the rally continues with players circling the court.
A player who misses loses a life; three lives each.
When two players are left, they play a point from the baselines to decide the winner.
Second game: run the other way round.
coaching_points: Hit high and deep so the rally keeps going and you have time to run.
Run round the net post, never across the court.
Be ready at the front of the queue with the racket back; the ball is coming as soon as you arrive.
Call 'mine' as you step in so nobody hits together.
progressions: Balls must land past the service line.
Two balls in play at once, started from both ends.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Allow two bounces before the ball must be hit.
Play across the service boxes only.
Five lives each instead of three.

name: Target Tennis: Hit the Cone, Win the Game
summary: Half-court points where hitting a cone with the ball wins the whole game outright, whatever the score.
setup: Two players rallying down one half of the court, lengthways. Three cones on each side, spread across the half two metres inside the baseline. Basket at the net post.
instructions: Rally cooperatively down the half for the first four balls, then the point is live; first to seven.
A ball that hits a cone on the fly or on its first bounce wins the game for the hitter, whatever the score.
A knocked-over cone is stood up by the player who hit it, before the next point.
Change ends after each game.
Second game: cones moved to a metre inside the service line so the targets are short.
coaching_points: Aim for the cone with a high ball; a low hard ball skips past it.
Keep the rally going first; the cone is a bonus, not the plan.
Recover to the middle of the half after each shot.
Hit through the ball towards the cone and hold the finish.
progressions: Two cones each side instead of three.
Only a cone hit on the first bounce counts.
Switch from a green ball to a yellow ball.
regressions: Five cones each side.
A cone hit on any bounce counts.
Use an orange ball.

name: Catch Ball Tennis
summary: A throw-and-catch team game across the net for the youngest players that teaches tracking, moving to the ball and calling it.
setup: Two teams, one each side of the net, inside the service boxes; cones on the singles sidelines at the service lines mark the area. Rackets are put down until the third game: the game is played by throwing and catching a red ball.
instructions: A player throws the ball underarm over the net into the other team's boxes.
The other team must catch it after one bounce; a catch means they throw it back, a drop or a ball out of the area is a point to the throwers.
First to ten points.
Second game: catches must be made before the bounce.
Third game: pick up the rackets, throw with the racket held in the other hand, and catch on the racket strings.
coaching_points: Throw underarm and high so the ball bounces up into the catcher's hands.
Catch with two hands in front of the body, eyes on the ball.
Move the feet to the ball before it bounces; do not reach.
Call 'mine' so two catchers do not go for the same ball.
progressions: Catches must be made before the bounce.
Use an orange ball.
Throw overarm instead of underarm.
regressions: Allow two bounces before the catch.
Throw from closer, a metre from the net.
Catch with the ball trapped against the chest.

name: Dice Tennis: Roll for the Rule
summary: Half-court games where a rolled or called number picks the rule for the next game from a list of six.
setup: Two players on one half of the court lengthways, with cones on the baselines and service lines at the centre line marking the half and a cone at the net post as the rule station. Six rules agreed out loud and numbered one to six: forehands only, backhands only, every ball past the service line, no ball harder than half pace, cross-court only, and one bounce then volley. Basket at the net post. A player calls a number with their eyes closed if there is no dice.
instructions: Before each game, roll or call a number; that rule applies to both players for the whole game.
Play a game to five points from a hand-feed under that rule; breaking the rule loses the point.
Roll again for the next game.
Play six games so every rule comes up at least once if possible.
With four players, the pair waiting keeps score and calls rule breaks.
coaching_points: Say the rule out loud before the first point; half the errors are forgetting it.
Forehands only: move around the backhand early.
Half pace: aim deeper, not softer.
Volley rule: after the bounce, move in behind your shot.
progressions: Two rules at once.
Games to seven points instead of five.
Start points from a serve.
regressions: Four rules only, leaving out the volley and cross-court rules.
Games to three points instead of five.
Cooperate for three balls before the point goes live.

name: Beat the Feeder: Ten Balls to Score Five
summary: A scoring game against the feeder where the hitter must land five of ten fed balls deep, with a leaderboard across the group.
setup: Feeder at the near net on the centre line with the basket, tossing to a hitter on the near baseline. The hitter aims over the net into the far court; a throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline marks the bonus zone. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder tosses ten balls, five to each side, at a steady rhythm.
Hitter scores one for every ball that lands past the far service line; the feeder wins the round if the hitter scores fewer than five.
Rotate the hitter after ten balls; keep a leaderboard.
